Title: A physics-guided deformable convolution with cross-scale kernel transfer for interpretable few-shot fault diagnosis of cylindrical roller bearings
Authors: Jinchuan Shi; Linlin Xue; Zhengkun Xue; Yukun Huang; Huageng Luo; Jian Li
Abstract: The vibration signal of a cylindrical roller bearing is a key carrier for its condition monitoring. The transient impacts and periodic modulation phenomena induced by bearing faults follow specific kinematics and impact. Purely data-driven deep learning models prioritize statistical correlations over physical laws, resulting in compromised reliability. This issue is compounded by sample scarcity and class imbalance, while the lack of physical interpretability limits diagnostic performance. Specifically, applying Deformable Convolutional Networks (DCN) directly to vibration signals can disrupt inherent physical mechanisms due to unconstrained spatial deformation, leading to overfitting. To address this, this paper proposes a physics-guided deformable convolutional (PGDC) neural network. First, a PGDC layer is designed to replace standard deformable convolution (DC), incorporating an impulse feature branch and four differentiable constraint losses (impulse, sparsity, smoothness, and periodicity) to explicitly embed fault priors into the learning process. Second, a cross-scale feature extraction mechanism driven by an impulse factor is developed, which evaluates channel-wise impulse sensitivity and propagates the most sensitive kernels across scales to ensure physical consistency of multi‑scale features. Third, an adaptive physics-constrained fusion framework is built to balance classification and constraint losses via a gating unit, enhancing generalization under small-sample and imbalanced data. Experiments in two groups of different cases were conducted. The results show that the proposed method achieves comprehensive F1 scores of 99.35% and 99.58% under K-fold cross-validation, outperforming mainstream comparison models. Results from t-SNE visualization and confusion matrices further indicate that the method extracts highly compact and interpretable fault features, improving the model’s diagnostic performance, generalization ability, and decision interpretability under small-sample and imbalanced data conditions.

Title: Anomaly detection method for hydro turbine units based on acoustic signals and improved CNN with Inception module
Authors: Xiong Xu; Zixin Li; Yong Xiong; He Wen; Haijun Lin
Abstract: Degradation in the health of hydro turbine units generates anomalous acoustic signals during operation. Accurate and stable anomaly detection of these operational acoustic signals is essential for unit health monitoring. However, traditional methods rely on manual feature extraction, which struggles to adapt to the complex acoustic environments characterized by high noise and time-varying conditions in hydropower stations. To address this, this paper proposes a convolutional neural network integrated with Inception modules (CNN-IM) for accurate anomaly detection of hydro turbine operational acoustic signals. Initially, convolutional layers perform preliminary feature extraction; subsequently, multi-scale Inception modules capture fault-related features across different temporal scales in parallel; then, an Efficient Channel Attention Network (ECA-Net) dynamically prioritizes fault-relevant channels and suppresses background noise; finally, fully connected layers achieve end-to-end fault classification. Extensive tests on datasets from actual hydropower stations demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method (highest accuracy of 97.17%) across various conditions, significantly outperforming comparative approaches such as the Training Interference Convolutional Neural Network (TICNN, 93.85%), One-Dimensional Deep Convolutional Neural Network (ODCNN, 89.50%), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP, 86.50%), highlighting its potential for reliable condition-based maintenance in hydro energy systems.

Title: A robust acoustic–vibration approach for early gear fault detection under modulation and broadband noise
Authors: Yaakoub Berrouche
Abstract: Early detection of incipient gear faults is a central problem in rotating-machinery health monitoring, particularly when fault signatures are low-amplitude and masked by modulation and broadband noise. We present the Local Damage Mode Extractor (LDME), a layered signal processing pipeline that chains four established operators in a principled order: (i) dual-path denoising via discrete wavelet transform (DWT) with adaptive Savitzky–Golay (SG) smoothing; (ii) Teager–Kaiser Energy Operator (TKEO) pre-amplification; (iii) Hadamard–Caputo (HC) fractional filtering of explicit discrete form and fixed order β=0.45; and (iv) harmonic-aware Fourier condition indicators combined by an unsupervised median-absolute-deviation (MAD) anomaly detector. The contribution of this work is not any single new operator but rather (a) the specific operator composition and the operator-theoretic rationale for its ordering, (b) a complete, parameter-explicit description that permits independent implementation, and (c) a controlled evaluation on two public benchmarks with threshold-sensitivity analysis. We evaluate LDME on the CWRU bearing dataset and on the HUMS 2023 planetary gearbox benchmark against five baselines spanning time- synchronous averaging, spectral kurtosis, variational mode decomposition, and cyclostationary analysis. On the HUMS 2023 dataset LDME raises a sustained detection alarm at cycle 198 versus cycle 284 for HT-TSA and cycle 355 for PLANET-TSA under identical threshold calibration. A threshold sensitivity analysis confirms that the detection-cycle ordering is preserved over a ±20% variation in the detection threshold. We discuss limitations, state where claims remain conjectures rather than theorems, and outline theoretical directions required to elevate the framework to a provably optimal detector.

Title: A lightweight and robust anomaly detection framework for High-Dimensional dynamic industrial Systems: RIF
Authors: Fu Li; Wei Lv; Jinhua Tan
Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) provides a critical data foundation for intelligent manufacturing and predictive maintenance, where anomaly detection is essential for ensuring reliable industrial operation. However, IIoT data are often high-dimensional, imbalanced, noisy, incomplete, and dynamically evolving, which limits the robustness and deployability of existing anomaly detection methods. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight and robust anomaly detection framework, termed Robust Isolation Forest (RIF), for high-dimensional dynamic industrial systems. Built upon the Isolation Forest paradigm, RIF integrates three coordinated mechanisms: Multi-Scale Feature Extraction (MSFE) for constructing reliable feature subspaces, Multi-dimensional Random Hyperplane Isolation (MRHI) for improving the separation of sparse anomalies, and Dynamic Weighted Ensemble Learning (DWEL) for adapting anomaly scoring to evolving data distributions. Experiments on the AI4I predictive maintenance dataset and a wind turbine SCADA dataset show that RIF achieves detection performance comparable to Extended Isolation Forest (EIF) on AI4I, while maintaining stable performance under missing-data perturbations. On the SCADA dataset, RIF improves over EIF in terms of F1-score and AUC-ROC, although false-positive control in complex continuous industrial processes remains challenging. Overall, RIF provides a unified and computationally efficient framework that balances detection performance, robustness, and computational complexity, offering a practical solution for robust anomaly detection in high-dimensional dynamic industrial environments.

Title: Fault detection and diagnosis in photovoltaic systems using artificial intelligence and time–frequency analysis
Authors: Abdellatif Seghiour; Yacine Bendjeddou; Imene Meriem Mostefaoui; Aissa Chouder; Hisham Alharbi; Abdullah S.Bin Humayd; Abebe Wondiferaw Wondimeneh; Abdulrahman Babqi
Abstract: This research introduces a novel artificial intelligence (AI) framework for fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) in photovoltaic (PV) systems that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with time–frequency analysis via the Wigner–Ville Distribution (WVD). The proposed method transforms raw numerical measurements—including solar irradiance, temperature, voltage, current, and power—into compact 6 × 12 time–frequency image representations, enabling effective spatial feature extraction by CNNs that are well suited to image-like data. The framework is benchmarked under both noiseless and noisy conditions on a comprehensive 17‑class dataset comprising one healthy condition (C0) and sixteen fault types (F1–F16), including progressive short‑circuit faults within a single string, pure partial‑shading faults, and combined inter‑string short‑circuit and asymmetric partial‑shading patterns along PV strings. To contextualize performance, the CNN–WVD model is compared not only with classical Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) but also with Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), Random Forests (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and k‑Nearest Neighbors (kNN), all trained on the same WVD‑transformed data. In noiseless conditions, ANN and DNN achieve 99.51% and 99.49% accuracy, respectively, while the CNN attains 97.09%; RF, SVM, GBM, and kNN reach 93.47%, 88.62%, 84.01%, and 75.69% accuracy. Under noisy conditions that emulate real PV environments, the CNN is the most robust model with 90.27% accuracy, outperforming ANN (82.20%), RF (82.80%), SVM (83.85%), GBM (73.85%), DNN (76.27%), and kNN (72.80%). Key contributions include: (i) the use of WVD to obtain highly informative time–frequency representations of PV electrical signals, (ii) a structured data‑organization strategy that maps multivariate PV measurements into fixed‑size WVD images, and (iii) a CNN architecture that preserves high discrimination capability across closely related fault severities and locations, even in the presence of noise achieving 90.8% accuracy under realistic sensor noise (baseline uncertainty: irradiance, temperature, voltage, current, power) and maintaining 71.5% accuracy at noise, representing extreme aging sensor conditions. With a competitive degradation of only 8.91 percentage points—lower than the neural-network baselines (ANN: 16.27%, DNN: 15.00%) and the tree ensemble RF (11.34%)—the CNN + WVD framework demonstrates superior noise robustness for long-term deployment in real-world PV installations. By bridging advanced time–frequency analysis with deep learning and systematically comparing against a broad set of machine‑learning baselines, the proposed framework enables fully automated, fine‑grained PV fault classification without manual feature engineering, thereby enhancing monitoring reliability, reducing downtime, and supporting predictive maintenance in large‑scale PV deployments.

Title: A multistage transfer learning framework for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery under variable operating conditions
Authors: Muhammad Farooq Siddique; Wasim Zaman; Muhammad Khalid; Bayan Hamdan; Jong Myon Kim
Abstract: The transition of industrial maintenance toward intelligent and autonomous operation requires non-destructive evaluation frameworks that remain reliable under variable operating conditions and limited labeled data. In practical inspection scenarios, data driven diagnostic models often suffer from performance degradation due to changes in operating speed and insufficient fault samples, which restrict their applicability in real machinery monitoring. To address this challenge, this study presents a multistage transfer learning framework designed to enhance vibration-based fault evaluation of rotating machinery under varying rotational speeds. The proposed framework progressively adapts a pretrained convolutional network through generic feature learning, vibration specific representation refinement, and task focused fine tuning, enabling stable feature reuse while preserving inspection relevant signal characteristics. A layer selective adaptation strategy is employed to retain general low-level representations while refining higher level features that capture speed dependent fault signatures. Experimental investigations conducted on vibration signals acquired from a milling machine operating at five spindle speeds demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves consistent and reliable fault discrimination across operating conditions, with classification accuracy ranging from 97.70% to 100%. The results indicate improved separation of fault induced time frequency patterns compared with conventional single stage transfer strategies. By enhancing robustness to operating variability and reducing dependence on extensive labeled datasets, the proposed framework contributes to reliable nondestructive evaluation and supports practical deployment of vibration-based condition monitoring systems in industrial environments.

Title: CyclicalNet: A Dense-Connected Architecture for Multiscale Cyclic Feature Learning in Planetary Gearbox Fault Diagnosis
Authors: Chaojun Xu; Yaqiang Jin; Junxiao Ma; Yuhao Wu; Peng Chen; Ge Xin; Changbo He
Abstract: Planetary gearboxes, crucial for industrial applications like wind turbines, automobiles, and robotics, are susceptible to failures due to complex vibrations and harsh conditions, making the development of effective fault diagnosis methods essential. While general-purpose deep learning models—such as Transformers, ResNets, DenseNets, and generative adversarial networks (GANs)—have shown promise in identifying intricate patterns within time series data for fault diagnosis, conventional one-dimensional convolutional kernels have inherent limitations, as they can only capture features from adjacent time series points. Additionally, methods that utilize attention mechanisms often struggle to uncover consistent dependencies among sparse data points that may be concealed within complex patterns. This paper introduces CyclicalNet, an innovative deep learning architecture designed to address these fundamental limitations in planetary gearbox fault diagnosis. The architecture uniquely integrates cyclical blocks, encoder blocks, and dense connections to process high amplitude–frequency components, traditionally overlooked in conventional models. A strategic reshape operation transforms one-dimensional sequential data into two-dimensional representations, enabling more structured and efficient feature extraction while facilitating simultaneous modeling of temporal and periodic features. The incorporation of dense connections promotes multiscale feature learning and enhances information flow across the network, resulting in richer and more discriminative feature representations. Through comprehensive experimental evaluation on planetary gearbox datasets, CyclicalNet demonstrates superior performance in fault diagnosis accuracy compared to existing methods, establishing a new benchmark in predictive maintenance technology.

Title: An efficient deep attention framework for multi-rotor UAVs fault diagnosis
Authors: Md Najmul Mowla; Davood Asadi; Mohammad Khaneghaei; Ferdous Sohel
Abstract: Motor faults in multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) jeopardize flight integrity and mission safety; practical operations require real-time detection with reliable severity estimation. Existing diagnostic frameworks struggle with nonlinear, noise-prone telemetry, often lack robust temporal modeling, and underperform at severity classification while being too heavy or unstable for onboard use. We introduce an enhanced multi-head self-attention mechanism-convolutional-LSTM network (EMHSAM-CLN), a compact deep attention framework that couples a convolutional-recurrent backbone with an enhanced multi-head self-attention mechanism for stable, noise-robust sequence modeling and efficient onboard inference. We develop a high-fidelity six-degrees-of-freedom (6-DoF) simulation dataset with graded motor faults (5-40% thrust reduction), realistic sensor noise (e.g., gyroscope: 0.01 deg/s; accelerometer: 0.4×10<sup>−3</sup> g), and mission phases spanning takeoff, hover, waypoint tracking, and landing. It outperforms strong attention baselines (+4.28 percentage points (pp) versus a convolutional-block attention variant; +6.15 pp versus a standard multi-head self-attention (MHSA) variant) and classical machine learning (+6.77 pp versus extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost)). Ablations attribute an absolute accuracy gain of 4.43 pp to the entire architecture relative to the best non-attention variant. These results indicate that EMHSAM-CLN provides a severity-aware and computationally compact framework for intelligent UAV health monitoring. Real-time feasibility is supported by the reported complexity and CPU-based runtime profiling; embedded SWaP validation (latency, peak memory, and power) remains a key direction for future work.

Title: Digital Twin-based framework for real-time fault diagnosis and prognosis of industrial robots using unsupervised learning and real experimental data
Authors: Ilhem Ben Hnaien; Eric Gascard; Zineb Simeu-Abazi; Hedi Dhouibi
Abstract: Industrial robotic systems require reliable predictive maintenance strategies to prevent unexpected failures and production downtime. Digital Twin (DT) technology supports industrial asset monitoring through synchronization between physical systems and their digital replicas. However, many existing DT-based diagnostic frameworks rely on simulated datasets or supervised learning models that require large fault-labeled datasets, which limits robustness in real industrial environments. This paper proposes the Digital Twin–Autoencoder Framework for Remaining Useful Life Estimation (DT-AE-RUL framework) for real-time fault diagnosis and prognostics in industrial robotic manipulators. The DT-AE-RUL framework integrates a calibrated Digital Twin model of the Stäubli TX60 robot with joint-specific unsupervised autoencoders trained exclusively on nominal operational data. Anomaly detection based on reconstruction error identifies abnormal behavior, while a degradation trend model estimates the Remaining Useful Life of robotic joints. Experimental results show an average detection delay of 0.02 s, a fault identification accuracy from 98 to 100%, and RUL prediction errors below 5%. These results demonstrate that the DT-AE-RUL framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient solution for predictive maintenance in industrial robotic systems.

Title: ConvECA-Net: A lightweight convolutional neural network for fault diagnosis of tapered roller bearings
Authors: Rishab Sahni; T. Narendiranath Babu
Abstract: The paper focuses on detecting faults in tapered roller bearings to prevent unplanned shutdowns, accidents, and financial losses. Title: Explainable LSTM-AdamW based fault diagnosis of aircraft rotating components using airborne acoustic signals under dynamic operating conditions
Authors: Yıldırım Özüpak; Emrah Aslan; Ievgen Zaitsev
Abstract: Acoustic signal (AS) has emerged as a powerful non-contact technique for early detection of incipient faults in aircraft rotating components due to its high sensitivity to transient damage mechanisms. The framework leverages sequential learning to capture the temporal evolution of acoustic signals and is systematically compared with conventional recurrent architectures, including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). The explainability analysis reveals that classification decisions are driven by localized, physically meaningful transient acoustic patterns associated with fault-induced events. In addition, a Taylor diagram–based statistical assessment confirms strong agreement between model predictions and reference signals, indicating robust preservation of temporal signal characteristics. The results suggest that the proposed explainable LSTM–AdamW framework provides a reliable, computationally efficient, and interpretable solution for acoustic signal-based fault diagnosis in aerospace applications, with strong potential for real-time condition monitoring and predictive maintenance.

Parallel multi-scale residual convolutions extract heterogeneous spatial fault signatures, while a Bidirectional LSTM encoder explicitly models the chronological sequence of mechanical-hydraulic transient events within the diagnostic window. Evaluated on a comprehensive multimodal pump dataset using a strict sequence-based train-test data split to prevent data leakage, the proposed framework achieves a classification accuracy of 99.60%, a Macro G-mean of 99.73%, and an AUC of 0.9999. The empirical results confirm that the proposed multi-sensor fusion strategy successfully disentangles complex degradation patterns, offering a highly reliable methodology for the intelligent condition monitoring of critical hydraulic machinery.

Title: Acoustic-based fault diagnosis of electric motors using Mel spectrograms and convolutional neural networks
Authors: Hasan Uzel; Yıldırım Özüpak; Feyyaz Alpsalaz; Emrah Aslan; Ievgen Zaitsev
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive deep learning framework for diagnosing acoustic faults in electric motors. The framework uses Mel spectrograms and a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN). The method classifies three motor states, engine_good, engine_broken, and engine_heavyload, based on audio recordings from the IDMT-ISA-ELECTRIC-ENGINE dataset. To prevent data leakage and ensure a robust evaluation, the study employed file-level splitting, session separation, 5-fold cross-validation, and repeated trials. The raw audio signals were transformed into Mel spectrograms and processed through a CNN architecture that integrates convolutional, pooling, normalization, and dropout layers. Quantitative metrics, including THD, spectral entropy, and SNR, further characterize the acoustic distinctions between motor states. The proposed model achieved a test accuracy of 99.7%, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art approaches, such as ResNet-18, CRNN, and Transformer classifiers, as well as traditional MFCC-based baselines. Noise robustness and sensitivity analyses demonstrated stable performance under varying SNR conditions and preprocessing settings. Feature-importance maps revealed that low-frequency regions (0–40 Mel bins) were key discriminative components linked to physical fault mechanisms. Computational evaluation confirmed the model’s real-time feasibility on embedded hardware with low latency and a modest parameter count. Though primarily validated on one motor type, external-domain testing revealed strong adaptability. Future work may incorporate transfer learning or multimodal fusion. Overall, the proposed framework provides a highly accurate, interpretable, and efficient solution for real-time motor fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance in industrial environments.

Title: Relational spectral descriptors for multi-sensor vibration-based motor fault diagnosis
Authors: Huy Hoang Nguyen; Tien Dung Do; Anh Hoang; Duc Chinh Hoang
Abstract: Multi-sensor vibration monitoring is important for industrial electric motors operating within coupled drivetrains (e.g., motor–pump assemblies) because faults affect not only local vibration energy but also transmission relationships between measurement locations. However, many existing approaches either rely on isolated handcrafted features or use deep models that treat sensor channels as independent stacked inputs, without explicitly modeling inter-sensor coupling. To address this limitation, we introduce a relational spectral descriptor that represents each vibration window using compact node-level statistics together with pairwise descriptors derived from multi-band magnitude-squared coherence and cross-spectral phase. Speed-aware frequency bands and coherence-based gating are incorporated to preserve diagnostically meaningful coupling while suppressing weak interactions. The resulting representation can be used by both vectorized and structured downstream learners, allowing the contribution of the descriptor itself to be separated from that of the downstream learning architecture. We evaluate the proposed descriptor under a strict grouped record-level anti-leakage protocol on the public 4TU motor–pump dataset and the public Machinery Fault Database (MAFAULDA), with the strong handcrafted ITSF+WPT baseline reported directly under the same main protocol rather than only in an auxiliary setting. Under in-distribution evaluation, FLAT_MLP_REL reaches 99.14% mean test macro-F1 on 4TU (mean of three random seeds), with MAIN_GNN reaching 99.10%, outperforming ITSF+WPT at 92.95%; on MAFAULDA, the same descriptor design transfers without modification and reaches 99.58% mean test macro-F1. Under a harder 4TU cross-folder protocol, the flat relational descriptor achieves 72.35% macro-F1, outperforming a raw-signal 1D-CNN baseline evaluated under the same protocol. A preliminary descriptor-level anti-noise evaluation and a cross-severity generalization study on MAFAULDA further illustrate the operating envelope of the proposed representation. Together, these results indicate that explicit spectral coupling provides a compact, interpretable, and practically useful representation for multi-sensor industrial fault diagnosis.

Title: Predictive maintenance in agricultural machinery: Activity-aware anomaly detection with language model-generated synthetic faults
Authors: Paolo Lindia; Riccardo Cantini; Francesco Bettucci; Luigi Sartori; Paolo Trunfio
Abstract: The increasing digitalization of agricultural machinery within the Agriculture 4.0 paradigm has led to widespread deployment of smart tractors equipped with high-frequency, geo-referenced sensors. These systems generate large volumes of multivariate time-series data, creating new opportunities to enhance operational reliability. However, anomaly detection in this context remains challenging due to high data dimensionality, spatiotemporal complexity, strong context dependence of faults, and limited labeled failure data. To address these challenges, this work proposes a spatiotemporal anomaly detection framework that integrates terrain- and activity-specific autoencoders with a synthetic anomaly generation pipeline powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Tractor sensor data are partitioned by terrain and clustered to uncover recurring activity patterns, enabling fine-grained, context-aware anomaly detection. To overcome the lack of real fault data, we introduce an LLM-driven, rule-based approach to generate realistic synthetic anomalies for systematic testing. The framework is validated on multivariate time-series data collected from the Controller Area Network bus of a New Holland T7.165 S tractor operating under diverse agricultural conditions. Experimental results show that context-specific autoencoders achieve high detection accuracy across a range of operational scenarios, while LLM-generated synthetic faults enable robust evaluation. Overall, by combining context-aware anomaly detection with LLM-driven fault generation, the proposed framework enhances predictive maintenance in precision agriculture and provides an effective approach to improving the reliability of modern agricultural machinery.

Title: Multi-task U-Net with class-conditional Mahalanobis scoring for drone acoustic anomaly detection
Authors: Jeongin Ju; Jungyu Choi; Seowoo Kim; Sungbin Im
Abstract: With the growing use of drones, early detection of abnormal operating conditions has become increasingly important. However, collecting representative fault examples before deployment is often difficult, making anomaly-label-free anomalous sound detection (ASD) practical for drone health monitoring. Anomaly scores are then computed as operating-condition-conditional Mahalanobis distance (MD) scores whose statistics are estimated only from normal training embeddings. Gradient-based losses, input-normalization statistics, and normal-reference estimation use normal training samples. Drone-type and flight-direction metadata supervise the auxiliary objectives and define the conditional reference groups. Labeled evaluation data are used for hyperparameter optimization, learning-rate scheduling, early stopping, and checkpoint selection, whereas the test set is reserved for final reporting. On the ICSV31-AI Challenge dataset, the full configuration achieved a test macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (Macro AUC) of 0.9592 ± 0.0059 over five random seeds. In the matched representation–scoring analysis, the multi-task representation with conditional scoring achieved a Macro AUC of 0.9592 ± 0.0059, compared with 0.4833 ± 0.0378 for the single-task representation with global scoring. A reconstruction-plus-classification variant achieved 0.9588 ± 0.0048, indicating that operating-condition-supervised representation learning was the major empirically supported contributor, while the remaining auxiliary components showed mixed or seed-dependent effects. Predicted metadata reduced the Macro AUC to 0.9095 ± 0.0087, and an exploratory normal-training-score threshold analysis revealed substantial false-alarm rates. The results support condition-aware representation learning and conditional normal modeling while identifying limitations in metadata reliability, threshold calibration, and cross-domain generalization.

Title: A Novel Approach for Remaining Useful Life Prediction With Anomaly-Driven Detection and Deep Feature Transfer
Authors: Wan Zhang; Yingchao Zhao; Jaspreet S. Dhupia; Yadong Xu
Abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is crucial for the predictive maintenance and health management of mechanical transmission systems. Although data-driven RUL prediction methods have advanced significantly, three key challenges remain: (i) constructing a physically interpretable health indicator (HI) that is invariant to operating conditions yet sensitive to incipient degradation; (ii) achieving adaptive time to start prediction (TSP) detection that accommodates nonstationarity and controls false and missed alarms; and (iii) accurate and generalizable RUL prediction under cross-domain scenarios. To address these issues, a method combining unsupervised anomaly detection and deep feature transfer for TSP determination and RUL prediction is proposed. A residual health indicator is constructed from an expected trajectory learned by Gaussian process regression (GPR) on the healthy segment and a Mahalanobis distance (MD) deviation measure. For the first time, extreme value theory (EVT) is used to create dynamic thresholds for performance degradation analysis and TSP determination. During the RUL prediction phase, transfer component analysis (TCA) mitigates feature distribution discrepancies between source and target domains. A dual long short-term memory (dual-LSTM) network with L2 regularization is then employed for RUL prediction across two transfer tasks. Experimental validation on a public benchmark dataset and a laboratory run-to-failure bearing dataset demonstrates the superior predictive accuracy and generalization capability of the proposed approach compared to existing methods.

Title: Explainable machine learning for incipient anomaly detection in compact molten salt heat exchanger with overlapping feature distributions
Authors: Konstantinos Prantikos; Taeseung Lee; Thanh Q. Hua; Lefteri H. Tsoukalas; Alexander Heifetz
Abstract: High-temperature molten salt-cooled reactors (MSCRs) are a promising next-generation nuclear technology option, offering efficient power conversion and inherent safety features. However, the reliability of these systems depends on the robust operation of heat exchangers (HXs), which are susceptible to failure due to temperature gradients and channel plugging caused by fluid freezing. Conventional monitoring methods, relying on inlet and outlet measurements, lack the spatial resolution needed to detect early-stage faults. We propose a novel design of a compact salt-to-salt matrix-type HX design consisting of interleaved arrays of parallel tubes, with integrated synthetic fiber optic distributed temperature sensing (DTS) to enable localized detection of incipient faults. To evaluate performance of this design, we generate high-fidelity synthetic data using heat transfer computational modeling to simulate channel plugging, and introduce sensor noise for realistic modeling of measurements. The dataset comprises of 97% normal operation and 3% anomaly cases, with each anomaly class representing 1% of the data. These early anomalies result in overlapping temperature profiles between normal and faulty channels, producing a non-separable dataset that challenges traditional classification techniques. We benchmark eight supervised machine learning (ML) models and demonstrate that XGBoost achieves the highest performance. To improve transparency, we develop an explainability framework combining Shapley values and partially ordered sets (POSETs) to quantify and structurally analyze feature importance. This approach identifies both dominant predictors and ambiguous feature relationships, enhancing trust and interpretability. Our results highlight the potential of combining DTS and explainable ML with intelligent feature selection to improve predictive maintenance and ensure operational resilience in advanced nuclear systems.

Abstract: Acoustic signals emitted by electrical power equipment, such as transformers, generators, and circuit breakers, encode critical operational states. As the physical knowledge is implemented in machine learning, the proposed solution will be more robust and efficient in predictive maintenance in a complex industrial environment, and fault detection systems will be improved in the future.

Title: Construction and research of a data-driven model for early fault detection in rotating machinery

Title: A novel strategy for fault detection in aircraft active landing gear using observer based global motion analysis
Authors: Azeddine Ratni; Djamel Benazzouz; Mohammed Tsebia
Abstract: Reliable motion tracking in avionic systems is essential for flight safety and predictive maintenance. The approach exploits global aircraft motion, including bounce, pitch, and roll dynamics, to ensure consistent state estimation and reliable fault detection. Simulation results show that the residuals remain close to zero under healthy operating conditions and increase significantly in the presence of actuator faults, enabling effective anomaly detection. These results highlight that a properly designed Luenberger observer, when consistently integrated with the physical dynamics of the system, can provide an effective and simple alternative to more complex stochastic estimation methods while maintaining comparable performance in aerospace applications.

Title: A hybrid VMD-CNN-autoencoder approach for speed-invariant fault detection of parallel and angular misalignment in rotating machinery
Authors: N. Chandran; K. Sathish Kumar
Abstract: Early identification of unbalance and shaft misalignment is essential for averting unforeseen failures and minimizing maintenance expenses in rotor-bearing systems. Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers with early stopping were used to avoid overfitting and classify the faults. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid technique, which combines experimental and data-driven methods, provides a reliable and scalable solution for intelligent condition monitoring of variable-speed rotor-bearing systems.

Title: Fault detection and isolation method for gas turbines using self-organizing type-3 fuzzy wavelet neural networks
Authors: Nastaran Mehrabi Hashjin; Mohammad Hussein Amiri; Amin Beheshti; Maryam Khanian Najafabadi
Abstract: Fault detection and isolation (FDI) in gas turbines is pivotal to maximizing efficiency, avoiding catastrophic damage, and minimizing unplanned outages. First, we introduce a bell-shaped Type-3 membership function that enhances uncertainty handling. Second, we train a neuro-fuzzy architecture with a hybrid Adam–Unscented Kalman Filter optimizer for fast convergence. Third, we embed a self-organizing mechanism that grows and prunes rules adaptively, yielding compact models without sacrificing accuracy. These results, together with robustness to 20-dB SNR and rigorous five-fold cross-validation, demonstrate superior computational efficiency and make ST3FRWNN a practical, deployable solution for real-world gas-turbine health monitoring.

Abstract: Induction motors, which are widely used in domestic and industrial applications, often operate under harsh mechanical, electrical, and thermal conditions that can lead to unexpected faults. Results confirm that, while conventional feature processing techniques perform well for electrical fault diagnosis, only the proposed FFT-informed input effectively captures both electrical and mechanical fault patterns and maintains strong generalization across independent experiments. By integrating the selected FFT components and a cascading workflow, the framework achieves an overall testing accuracy of 98.28%, in contrast to 59.01% when FFT features are excluded and the diagnosis system operates as a simple 4-class classifier.

Experiments on the MNIST∼USPS object recognition anomaly detection and a real-world bearing dataset collected from a steel factory in China demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses false alarms. It achieves highly accurate and timely alarm triggering for online EFD, offering a robust and practical solution for industrial applications.

Title: Fault diagnosis technology of aero-engine based on self-adaptive time-frequency graph neural network approach of transfer for reliability improvement
Authors: Junfa Li; Youchao Sun; Hao Wang; Jingyi Xia

This significantly enhances the model’s ability to adapt to changes in operating conditions variations and its overall generalization performance across different conditions. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the target domain of the proposed ATFGDANet model is significantly better than that of the existing mainstream comparison methods in the cross-condition tasks of multiple data sets. Title: One-class deep feature extraction of nonlinear independent components for gearbox anomaly detection
Authors: Xiaoyun Gong; Mengxuan Hao; Chuan Li; Wenliao Du; Ziqiang Pu

To tackle this issue, a one-class deep feature extraction (OCDFE) method is put forward for gearbox condition monitoring using only health condition data. Specifically, nonlinear independent components are first estimated from normal vibration data. The estimated components are then encoded using deep convolutional autoencoder. Results show that the present method can effectively extract the anomaly features for different anomaly detectors. It can potentially differentiate the normal and abnormal features for gearbox anomaly detection.

Title: Multitask learning for robust incipient fault diagnosis in rotating machinery
Authors: Sofia Chergui; Rafik Medjoudj; Amir Aieb; Youcef Sklab; Nadir Bouzouba; Abderrazak Sebaa
Abstract: Interturn stator faults are among the most critical failure modes in induction motors: once an incipient fault progresses beyond its earliest stage, thermal runaway and irreversible insulation damage can occur within minutes. This work proposes LITE-SimpleVoltReg, a lightweight multitask deep learning framework for incipient fault diagnosis under varying voltage conditions. The model couples a multi-scale temporal backbone (Light Inception with Boosting Technique, LITE) with an auxiliary voltage regression head trained in parallel on the raw input features. Robustness is evaluated using a Leave-Voltage-Pair-Out protocol that trains on disjoint voltage ranges and tests on held-out ones, providing a rigorous out-of-distribution assessment. On 10-timestep sequences, LITE-SimpleVoltReg achieves 97.6% average accuracy across five voltage splits, outperforming adversarial domain generalization baselines by 5%–8% on the hardest splits while attaining statistically equivalent accuracy to methods with 30× more parameters. Performance remains strong at 93.6% and 94.4% on 20- and 30-timestep sequences. With fewer than 20k parameters, a 66 kilobyte memory footprint, and sub-millisecond inference latency, the model runs on standard low-cost microcontrollers without a dedicated graphics processing unit, offering a practical path towards scalable, embedded predictive maintenance in industrial motor fleets.

Title: Metrological characterization of beamforming-enhanced acoustic sensing for non-contact motor fault diagnosis
Authors: Yixiang Huang; Lyu Lyu
Abstract: Acoustic sensing provides a non-intrusive pathway for motor health monitoring, yet its application to motor fault diagnosis has been extremely limited. Title: A condition-guided non-invasive framework for health state assessment and anomaly warning of marine main engines using multi-cylinder exhaust gas temperature
Authors: Rui Wang; Guichen Zhang; Yuanlong Li; Wenjie Guo
Abstract: Marine main engines operate for prolonged periods under continuously varying speed and load conditions. Experiments on real operational data from an in-service bulk carrier show that LCG-HAN achieves accurate health baseline estimation and outperforms representative recurrent, attention-based, and persistence baselines. The proposed method identifies sustained candidate abnormal thermal-state episodes while reducing false alarms caused by transient noise, thereby providing interpretable monitoring cues for long-term shipboard condition assessment.

Title: Contrastive adversarial glow model for machinery anomaly detection and degradation assessment

Abstract: Rotating machinery typically operates in healthy state for long periods, leaving abnormal data scarce and making supervised condition monitoring models unreliable. Experiments on bearing and gas-turbine rotor datasets demonstrate that, the proposed CAGlow can produce markedly smoother metric curves during healthy operation, detect anomaly onset earlier with sharper responses, and achieve clear separation between distinct fault degradation stages, as compared with state-of-the-art methods.

Authors: Shuo Xing; Wenjie Bao; Changming Cheng; Dangpeng Jin; Xin Zhang; Songyong Liu
Abstract: As critical components of mechanical systems, bearing health conditions directly impacts production efficiency and operational safety, making accurate health monitoring essential for effective maintenance and risk reduction. In addition, discrepancies in feature distributions across different equipment and operating conditions often lead to degraded diagnostic performance, especially under fluctuating speed conditions. Therefore, a multi-stage decoupling and fusion Transformer (MDFformer) is proposed, which is designed to progressively decouple multi-sensor signal features to extract key features that reflect the health condition of bearings, while simultaneously achieving cross-condition fault diagnosis. Firstly, a random orthogonal decoupling Transformer is designed, in which features from heterogeneous sensors are interactively decoupled and recalibrated during the initial feature extraction stage. Subsequently, a level-by-level guided decoupling Transformer for multi-sensor features is constructed to progressively extract the interactive information between multi-sensor and fused features, thereby achieving the layer-by-layer decoupling and fusion of multi-sensor signal features. Finally, cross-condition fault diagnosis is achieved through adversarial training and a feature distribution discrepancy minimization strategy. Experimental results indicate that MDFformer delivers superior and robust diagnostic performance in cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis, with diagnostic accuracies exceeding 99% under fluctuating speed conditions.

Existing deep learning methods typically rely on single-scale temporal features, often failing to capture transient disturbances and long-term degradation patterns simultaneously. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Transformer (MSFF-Transformer) specifically designed for industrial temporal fault diagnosis. The model adopts a three-channel feature extraction framework using a consistent sliding window strategy to generate instantaneous representations, time-domain statistical indicators, and frequency-domain spectral features via Fast Fourier Transform. Each feature stream is processed by a dedicated Transformer encoder, enabling scale-specific decoupled modeling to prevent feature interference. Then, a dynamic gated attention-based fusion mechanism integrates heterogeneous information by adaptively evaluating the reliability of each channel. Furthermore, the model maintains stable performance across four industrial scenarios: mild and severe Gaussian noise, quantization, and sensor drift. For instance, under severe Gaussian noise, it maintains an accuracy of 0.945, while the standard Transformer drops to 0.885. These results indicate that combining multi-scale decoupled modeling with adaptive global sequence modeling improves diagnostic accuracy and robustness, providing a practical and efficient solution for intelligent condition monitoring in complex energy systems.

Title: Asymmetric stochastic-resonance spiking ResNet for noise-robust cross-domain fault diagnosis of mining machinery
Authors: Miaomiao Yang; Hongfei Duan; Hongzhi Song; Xining Ren; Lijuan Zhao; Zhiyong Yang; Dayu Ye; Xiang Meng
Abstract: Reliable fault diagnosis for mining machinery is challenged by three coupled factors: (i) weak fault signatures obscured by heavy noise; (ii) labeled data are exceedingly scarce owing to the high cost and inherent risks of collecting fault samples; and (iii) substantial distribution shifts between source and target domains induced by rapidly changing operating conditions. In the context of Industry 4.0 predictive maintenance, this task is an application of artificial intelligence for maintaining automated industrial equipment before faults cause downtime or safety incidents. We propose an asymmetric stochastic-resonance deep spiking residual network (ASR-DSRN), a noise-robust cross-domain framework that addresses these factors jointly. The model integrates (1) an asymmetric stochastic-resonance (ASR) front-end embedded within a residual spiking network to selectively amplify subthreshold periodic components while preserving temporal sparsity; (2) a discrete wavelet transform-based downsampling block with spectral attention (DWT-DS) that decomposes features into multiresolution subbands and adaptively reweights informative frequencies; and (3) a transfer-learning scheme that couples transfer frequency-centered kernel alignment (TFCKA) with a time–wavelet domain discrimination loss (TWDL) to support label-free source–target alignment and class separation in both time and wavelet views. Experiments on bearing and planetary gearbox datasets under strong noise and cross-speed/load transfer settings demonstrate consistent gains over competitive convolutional neural network, artificial neural network, and spiking baselines. These results validate the integrated design and highlight ASR-DSRN as a practical artificial-intelligence solution for noise-robust, label-efficient, cross-domain fault diagnosis in mining-machinery predictive maintenance.

Title: An intelligent fault diagnosis method for rolling bearings integrating multi-level feature extraction and supervised geometry and statistics-preserving embedding
Authors: Wenhao Yang; Xiaoli Qi; Zhiwen Wang; Dehai Cui; Fangxiang Zhao; Dengcheng Luo
Abstract: In industrial condition monitoring systems, accurate and robust fault diagnosis of rotating machinery in complex environments remains a critical challenge. Existing deep learning models, such as StarNet, often suffer from insufficient feature representation, information loss during pooling, and inadequate loss functions that fail to capture intra-class and inter-class relationships. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel network model based on PGStarNet-MFE and SWD-GSE. Firstly, a novel multi-head feature extraction (MFE) module is constructed using a multi-scale convolutional architecture to achieve hierarchical feature representation of time-frequency maps, thereby significantly enhancing the network’s feature extraction capability. Secondly, a supervised Sliced Wasserstein Distance-Geometry and Statistics-preserving Manifold Embedding (SWD-GSE) dimensionality reduction algorithm is designed to replace the traditional average pooling layer. This algorithm introduces a geometric structure preservation mechanism during feature space reduction, retaining critical diagnostic information. Finally, a linearly weighted loss function (PGLF) based on an improved Greater Cane Rat Algorithm is proposed to optimize feature space distribution via correlation modeling. The proposed approach is evaluated on three bearing datasets, and its performance compared with alternatives. Experimental results show the framework consistently achieves superior diagnostic accuracy and robustness. This study offers a novel pathway for intelligent bearing diagnosis under complex conditions.

Title: Semantic-driven dynamic graph learning for wind turbine gearbox anomaly detection
Authors: Ying Xie; Jixiang Wang; Rongbin Xu; Lijie Wen; Zhiqiang Xu; Junnan Shen; Yun Yang
Abstract: Supervisory control and data acquisition systems enable data-driven condition monitoring of wind turbine gearboxes. The high-dimensional and noisy data lead to inefficient feature selection, which weakens prediction accuracy and undermines the reliability of downstream anomaly detection. To address these challenges, we present a novel Semantic-Driven Dynamic Graph Learning (SDDGL) framework that infuses domain semantics into graph-based spatial-temporal modeling. It begins by transforming variables into semantic vector representations to detect meaningful clusters and filter out irrelevant noise. These features are embedded into a dynamic autoencoder that captures temporal and spatial dynamics. It tracks evolving behaviors through graph learning with hybrid temporal modeling. To enhance detection robustness under complex operational dynamics, SDDGL promotes consistency in learned representations and leverages error analysis. Experimental results in two wind farms demonstrate that SDDGL outperforms baseline models, achieving a Receiver Operating Characteristic-Area Under the Curve of 0.902 and 0.909. These results highlight the robust and efficient performance in gearbox anomaly detection. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/YingXie/SDDGL to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

Title: Interpretable graph neural networks for wind turbine fault feature identification with physics-based constraints and self-supervised pretraining
Authors: Shulei Xue; Yanling Lv; Yang Liu
Abstract: Rule-based Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) alarm schemes in wind farms exhibit limited adaptability and excessive redundancy. Meanwhile, SCADA measurements are highly imbalanced: normal operating conditions dominate, whereas fault samples are scarce. This imbalance has biased data-driven models toward the normal class and has increased missed alarms. To address these challenges, a physics-informed, interpretable spatio-temporal graph neural network with self-supervised pretraining (PhysIP-STGNN) was proposed for wind turbine operating-state recognition and decision support for typical component fault diagnosis. First, following the principles of component relevance and functional consistency, SCADA variables were aggregated into a set of monitorable nodes to establish the basis for model training. Second, by integrating a physics-prior graph with a data-driven causal graph, the structural backbone of the model and condition-dependent causal relations were constructed, and a graph-attention mechanism was employed to learn structured spatio-temporal representations. In addition, power-curve consistency and thermal-balance mechanisms were injected into the learning process as soft constraints. A graph–temporal masked reconstruction pretraining strategy was further developed to exploit unlabeled time windows and improve representation robustness under limited labelled fault samples. Experiments were conducted using real operational data collected from a wind farm in Heilongjiang, China. PhysIP-STGNN achieves a macro-averaged F1-score (Macro-F1) of 96.81%. Compared with six baselines, PhysIP-STGNN achieves the best overall performance and improves Macro-F1 by 2.96 percentage points over the strongest baseline, Transformer. Moreover, engineering-oriented diagnostic evidence graphs are produced to support condition monitoring and operation-and-maintenance decision-making for wind turbines.

Title: An incremental learning framework with dynamic replay and graph attention for unknown fault detection in aviation bearings
Authors: Chenjian Jia; Jing Tang; Junxian Shen
Abstract: The health monitoring of aviation bearings is critical to flight safety. However, practical deployment faces three major challenges: (1) the need to continuously process unlabeled data streams to autonomously perceive and diagnose emerging faults; (2) the catastrophic forgetting problem inherent in incremental learning, which requires the system to stably retain acquired knowledge during this process; and (3) the stringent memory and computational constraints of onboard systems. To address these challenges, a Dynamic Replay and Incremental Fault Detection framework with Graph-based Incremental Learning (DRIFT-GIL) was developed in this study. First, an unsupervised drift detection mechanism using multi-sensor power spectral entropy distribution features (derived from the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) power spectrum) was established to identify new fault states in real-time. Second, multi-sensor spatio-temporal graphs were built by mapping time-series segments into graph nodes, which accurately characterizes the spatio-temporal correlations of fault evolution, and employs Graph Attention Networks for deep feature encoding. Third, to mitigate catastrophic forgetting, we propose a collaborative optimization mechanism. This mechanism specifically integrates an intelligent replay strategy based on representative samples and a meta-learned hybrid loss function. This mechanism facilitates knowledge distillation through a teacher-student model in the graph embedding space, enabling the system to acquire new fault knowledge while consolidating historical fault representations with fewer replay samples. Validation on two aviation bearing test rigs shows that DRIFT-GIL effectively identifies unknown faults, achieving average diagnostic accuracies of 99.08% and 98.88%. Versus full-data training, the framework reduces average replay samples by 82.10%, balancing accuracy and efficiency for aviation monitoring.

Title: An uncertainty-aware deep neural network framework integrated with adapted engine modeling for robust sensor fault detection in aero gas turbine engines: validation using flight test data
Authors: Sangjo Kim
Abstract: This study proposes an uncertainty-aware deep neural network (DNN) framework integrated with adapted engine modeling for robust sensor fault detection in aero gas turbine engines. In practical applications, sensor fault detection is challenged by the absence of true reference values and the presence of engine-to-engine performance variation caused by manufacturing tolerances, degradation, and maintenance conditions. To address this limitation, a physics-based engine model is employed to generate large-scale datasets incorporating component performance uncertainty. These analytically generated datasets are used to train DNN models that learn the nonlinear relationship between operating conditions and expected sensor behavior under healthy conditions. A key feature of the proposed approach is that no flight test data are used during model training. The model is trained exclusively on simulation-based datasets, eliminating the need for large volumes of experimentally accumulated data. The trained models are first evaluated using simulation datasets not used during training, demonstrating strong regression performance with normalized root mean squared errors below approximately 1.5% under ±1% component performance variation. To validate real-world applicability, flight test data are used solely for independent validation and are not involved in the training process. Sensor fault scenarios are constructed by introducing controlled bias errors into measured signals. When evaluated on these flight test–based datasets, the model achieves classification accuracies of 93.4%, 93.5%, and 87.5% for DNN models trained under ±1%, ±3%, and ±5% component performance variation, respectively. Furthermore, because the proposed method relies only on a pre-trained DNN model during operation, no physics-based engine model is required in the on-board environment. This enables fast and stable inference suitable for real-time applications. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully generalizes from simulation-based training to real-world conditions while maintaining reliable sensor fault detection performance. These characteristics make the approach highly suitable for practical digital twin and real-time health monitoring applications in aero gas turbine engines.

Title: Offshore drilling motor diagnostics using dual-point downhole measurement and early fault detection via a genetic-algorithm–optimized neural network
Authors: Jiahao Zhan; Jun Li; Hongwei Yang; Chao Wang; Biao Wang; Zhenyu Long
Abstract: Positive Displacement Motors (PDM) in offshore drilling often fail without warning, causing costly downtime. Notably, conventional surface monitoring and theoretical models are inadequate in the presence of noisy signals and limited telemetry bandwidth. Therefore, this paper proposes a dual-point downhole measurement system with sensors placed above and below the motor, capturing input and output parameters simultaneously, enabling a comprehensive performance profile for data-driven analysis. Specifically, in the proposed model, a genetic-algorithm–optimized backpropagation neural network, trained on more than 1.5 million field samples from multi-well operations, provides real-time performance estimation and anomaly detection based on prediction-measurement residuals. This artificial intelligence approach enables automated condition monitoring without requiring explicit physical characterization of the motor. The developed model achieves mean relative errors of 2.02% for rotational speed and 5.71% for torque, outperforming traditional methods (5.83% and 29.57%). Furthermore, field case studies demonstrate that downhole anomaly alerts are issued approximately 2 h earlier than surface-based fault recognition, enabling proactive intervention. Designed for downhole deployment, the proposed system processes data locally and transmits compact health signals within bandwidth constraints. This integrated framework improves the reliability of offshore drilling motors, reduces downtime, and enhances operational safety. Its modular, data-driven design also supports adaptation to other rotating downhole tools, such as rotary steerable systems, and can be extended to broader offshore equipment monitoring.

Authors: T. Aravind; A. Hema Malini; C. T. Kalaivani; T. Archana
Abstract: This paper presents a unified smart-grid framework integrating solar forecasting, fault detection, and energy optimization using adaptive attention, federated learning, and quantum-inspired algorithms. The QINN–DHFD combination delivers 98% grid efficiency and 20% reduction in energy loss under fluctuating conditions. These results establish the proposed framework as a robust, scalable solution for enhancing sustainability and resilience in next-generation renewable energy systems.

Title: MIEI-DPMIAN: fault diagnosis for urban rail transit gearboxes based on torsional vibration signal image enhancement and attention network
Authors: Jiayao Hu; Wennian Yu; Kai Chen; Li Yu; Xiaoxi Ding; Wenbin Huang
Abstract: As the core component for power transmission in the traction system of urban rail transit trains, gearboxes require timely condition monitoring and diagnosis to ensure safe train operation. Currently, vibration measurement methods based on gearbox housings suffer from signal attenuation when gear impact vibrations propagate to the gearbox housing. Moreover, Pseudo-color images (PCIs) generated by direct encoding of existing one-dimensional (1D) signals have poor detail definition. Meanwhile, feature information from different branches of existing multi-scale models cannot interact effectively. To solve these problems, this study extracts the internal in-situ torsional vibration signals of gearboxes by decomposing the acceleration components measured by accelerometers. Then, a Matrix information expansion image (MIEI) coding method is developed. Before converting the matrix generated by 1D signal encoding into PCIs, the cross-covariance of matrix rows and columns is calculated to avoid color mapping of matrix elements, thereby realizing effective feature expansion and generating true-color images with more abundant feature details. In addition, the information enhancement mechanism of MIEI is analyzed using image information entropy. Furthermore, a Channel fusion reconstruction (CFR) module is designed, and a Dual-pool parallel multi-scale interactive attention network (DPMIAN) is proposed to achieve effective information interaction and accurate feature extraction. The proposed method achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 99.18% and shows better robustness compared with state-of-the-art image encoding methods and diagnostic models. Finally, public BJTU and MFPT datasets are employed to comprehensively verify the performance of MIEI and DPMIAN.

Title: Optimized lightweight ANN with domain-driven feature engineering for fault-diagnosis in grid-connected photovoltaic systems

Title: Attention-throughout: a latent diffusion approach for single domain generalization in machinery fault diagnosis
Authors: Yifan Wu; Chuan Li; Rui Liu; Dandan Zhao; Min Xia
Abstract: Domain Generalization (DG) has been explored to achieve machine fault diagnosis under previously unseen operating conditions. However, most DG methods assume access to training data collected across multiple conditions, an assumption that rarely holds in industrial practice, where fault data are typically available from only a single operating condition. To address this critical constraint, we propose an attention-throughout latent diffusion model for single-source domain generalization (ATLD-SSDG). The proposed framework learns discriminative fault representations from a single-condition source domain and generalizes robustly to multiple unseen target conditions. First, to effectively capture complementary fault information, vibration signals from three views are fused and projected into a latent space via a collaborative attention fusion mechanism. Next, a dedicated one-dimensional (1D) U-Net is constructed to address information loss in existing approaches and facilitate more effective conditional diffusion. Unlike existing methods that directly adopt computer vision diffusion architectures, the proposed 1D U-Net is specifically designed for vibration signals, preserving localized fault-related details and preventing information loss caused by time–frequency transformations. Moreover, by explicitly regulating self-attention and cross-attention within the diffusion model, the framework preserves fault-relevant characteristics while selectively substituting operating-condition-related factors, thereby enabling controllable and effective domain generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior generalization performance and diagnostic accuracy of the proposed method over state-of-the-art DG methods. These results indicate that latent diffusion, when properly structured for 1D condition-monitoring signals, provides an effective mechanism for single-source domain generalization, helping to close an important gap in DG research for predictive maintenance.

Title: ECViT: A novel domain incremental fault diagnosis framework for axial piston pump
Authors: Zhen Zhang; Xu Yang; Dong Han; Rulin Zhou; Lijie Jiang
Abstract: Online fault diagnosis for axial piston pump is crucial for ensuring safe equipment operation, but diverse working conditions result in performance degradation of diagnostic models. In this paper, an efficient cross-attention vision transformer (ECViT) is proposed to perform fault diagnosis of axial piston pump in the dynamic domain. First, a convolutional patch embedding (CPE) module is used to project the input sequence to different sizes and extract local features. Next, the extracted multi-scale features are fused through the proposed efficient cross-attention (ECA) module to enhance feature interaction. Subsequently, we design a condition-aware parameter adaptation (CAPA) module based on fuzzy membership functions, which infers operating condition labels for diagnosis instances and configures the corresponding model parameters. Finally, experiments were conducted on an axial piston pump test bench. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average accuracy of 99.83% over diverse domains, outperforming the comparative models. With the ability of adapting to diverse operating conditions and mitigating diagnostic performance degradation, the proposed method provides a reliable framework for online condition monitoring and intelligent fault diagnosis of axial piston pump.

Title: CrossSTLLM: A continually adaptive spatiotemporal large language model for anomaly detection and fault localization in wind turbines with diverse distribution
Authors: Qingtao Yao; Ruibin Ban; Ling Xiang; Xiaolong Wang; Aijun Hu; Hankun Bing
Abstract: Wind turbine SCADA data varies widely across sites and over time, resulting in cross-spatiotemporal heterogeneity and evolving operating conditions that can degrade traditional anomaly detectors. To address these challenges, a novel anomaly detection and fault localization framework is proposed, leveraging a continually adaptive cross-spatiotemporal large language model (CrossSTLLM) and a statistic indicator. CrossSTLLM adapts to spatiotemporal heterogeneity and concept drift through continual learning, thereby capturing evolving operational patterns and integrating new site-specific data distributions. During online operation, a condition monitoring indicator based on Hotelling's T<sup>2</sup> statistic is proposed for interpretable anomaly detection and fault localization. The multivariate outputs of CrossSTLLM are subjected to Hotelling's T<sup>2</sup>-based monitoring, yielding a unified deviation score for each time window. When this T<sup>2</sup> statistic exceeds a predefined control limit, an anomaly is declared and the contributions of individual sensors to the statistic are analyzed to localize the fault. In this manner, the anomalies are flagged and the SCADA variables driving abnormal behavior are identified. The approach is validated on SCADA data from two real wind farms, where CrossSTLLM provided early fault alerts 27 and 26 days before maintenance events. Quantitatively, CrossSTLLM achieved up to 39% lower RMSE and an R<sup>2</sup> of 0.990–0.994, outperforming advanced models. These results demonstrate a robust, generalizable solution for SCADA-based anomaly detection and early, interpretable fault localization across diverse wind turbine fleets.

Title: Transient-aware spectral segmentation informed by energy-distribution modeling and optimized band selection for railway bogie fault diagnosis
Authors: Peng Chen; Qingsheng Wei; Yazheng Wang; Ge Xin; Changbo He
Abstract: Bogie axle bearings, critical to high-speed train safety and performance, operate in challenging low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) environments–particularly affected by complex, broadband interference from track impacts and braking events. Current diagnostics struggle with random pulse noise-masked fault signatures, while decomposition methods face mode mixing issues, and deep learning approaches require extensive labeled data while lacking interpretability. We introduce Transient-Aware Spectral Segmentation (TASS), which models energy distributions and optimizes frequency-band selection to suppress broadband, nonstationary interference in bogie bearing signals. Central is Amplitude-Weighted Ordinal Entropy (AWOE), which reweights ordinal patterns by amplitude to localize transient noise and overcome the amplitude insensitivity of permutation entropy, enabling an entropy-guided decomposition that fuses spectral-envelope and entropy distributions for physically interpretable, impulse-robust segmentation. In parallel, particle swarm optimization with an Enhanced Spectral Energy Ratio (ESER) automatically selects fault-sensitive bands that emphasize characteristic frequencies and harmonics while penalizing broadband transients. Across operating regimes and sensing modalities (onboard and wayside), TASS increases effective SNR, improves detection reliability, and reduces false alarms, supporting engineering assurance and condition-based maintenance.

Title: An adaptive industrial large language model for mechanical fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions
Authors: Chaojun Xu; Zisheng Wang; Yaqiang Jin; Weihang Nong
Abstract: Under variable operating conditions, mechanical vibration signals exhibit strong nonlinearity and time-varying characteristics. Traditional signal processing and deep learning methods struggle to extract stable fault features, posing challenges to early equipment fault detection and health management. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Variable Operating Condition Large Language Model (VOC-LLM). The model builds a multidimensional vibration feature fusion module to embed time-domain statistical features, time–frequency domain entropy features and nonlinear dynamic features into the Transformer semantic space. It encodes variable-speed features to capture time-varying signal dependencies and designs lightweight adaptation for the large language model (LLM). This adaptation achieves efficient domain alignment with industrial scenarios while preserving pre-trained knowledge. The model deeply couples mechanical fault semantics with model inference logic to realize interpretable quantitative assessment of fault severity. Tested on both laboratory and industrial platforms, VOC-LLM significantly outperforms mainstream advanced methods. It accurately identifies equipment faults of varying severity levels, providing a practical and interpretable solution for predictive maintenance of industrial equipment.

Title: Weak anomaly detection of axial piston pumps by fusing information from simulated and measured pressure signals
Authors: Zhongrui Wang; Qun Chao; Wentao Wang; Zhiqiang Zhang; Chengliang Liu
Abstract: Axial piston pumps are crucial power components in hydraulic systems and their anomaly detection is essential for the condition monitoring of electro-hydraulic equipment. Discharge pressure signals are commonly used to assess the health condition of pumps due to their sensitivity to internal faults and availability in practical hydraulic systems. However, the anomaly detection of axial piston pumps using pressure signals is challenging due to the scarcity of faulty signals. To address this issue, this paper proposes a weak anomaly detection method based on information fusion of measured pressure signals and simulated ones, which requires no faulty training samples. The proposed framework addresses two critical challenges in similarity-based anomaly detection: the lack of standard references and the construction of effective metrics. First, the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model of an axial piston pump is built to generate simulated discharge pressure signals that serve as references. Second, a metric is constructed to evaluate the pump’s health condition by calculating the similarity between the weighted-graph (WG) matrices from reference and measured pressure signals. The comparative experiments show that the proposed method is the only method to achieve an accuracy of 100% in the task of weak anomaly detection for axial piston pumps. The clearance value of the proposed method reaches up to 0.145, outperforming existing methods by at least 0.17, verifying the sensitivity of the constructed similarity metric. The proposed method provides a reliable means to detect anomalies in axial piston pumps without need of faulty data.

Title: Intelligent fault detection of electric motor bearing using wavelet packet transform and ED-RBFNN
Authors: Hamed Helmi; Ahmad Forouzantabar; Mohammad Azadi
Abstract: The ubiquitous nature of electric motors across diverse industries highlights the critical role of components like rolling bearings in ensuring reliable operation. Bearing defects are a leading cause of rotating machinery failure, underscoring the importance of effective diagnostic methods. This research presents an intelligent system for rolling bearing fault detection in electric motors. The proposed system utilizes vibration analysis and Daubechies wavelet packet decomposition to extract approximate and detail signals across three levels. Innovatively, this research combines Wavelet Packet Transform (WPT) with an Enhanced Dynamic Radial Basis Function Neural Network (ED-RBFNN) for intelligent fault detection. The combination of WPT and ED-RBFNN provides adaptive and accurate fault detection; WPT decomposes signals to reveal subtle fault indicators, while ED-RBFNN dynamically learns and classifies these patterns, adapting to non-static conditions and offering robust feature extraction and dynamic learning. Extracted features, both in the time and frequency domains, are subjected to a distance evaluation method for feature selection, resulting in a feature vector that serves as input to the ED-RBFNN. The system, trained and tested on separate datasets, demonstrates high reliability and accuracy in detecting the presence and location of rolling bearing faults, effectively distinguishing between healthy and defective bearings. This robust solution for predictive maintenance in industrial settings serves as a valuable tool for minimizing downtime and improving the operational lifespan of rotating machinery, contributing to the development of advanced predictive maintenance techniques and ensuring reliable and efficient industrial operations.

Title: Adaptive distribution transformation for enhanced bearing fault detection in independent cart systems
Authors: Abdul Jabbar; Marco Cocconcelli; Gianluca D’Elia
Abstract: Unlike conventional rotary systems, where bearings remain fixed around a single axis and experience only rotational motion, bearings in independent cart systems exhibit coupled translational–rotational motion and highly nonstationary dynamics. This simultaneous translational-rotational motion of the bearings along the guide rail results in time-varying vibration signatures, complicating fault diagnosis using conventional methods. Furthermore, each cart in an independent cart system is supported by multiple rolling bearings, and industrial machines involve hundreds of carts operating simultaneously, resulting in a large number of interacting bearings whose condition monitoring is both challenging and highly desirable. This study proposes an adaptive distribution-based feature transformation method to enhance the detection of bearing faults under complex operating conditions. The proposed method effectively reshapes the skewed, bimodal, and high-variance feature distributions commonly observed in vibration signals from independent cart systems, thereby improving class separability without the need for labeled data or deep learning architectures. The approach was validated on the open-access bearing dataset based on independent cart systems comprising single- and three-cart experiments and benchmarked against established transformations including Box–Cox, Yeo–Johnson, Rotation-Based Iterative Gaussianization, hyperbolic power transformation, Cumulative Density Function - Transform-and-Shift, dip test based extraction, and Dip transformation. The results demonstrate that the proposed transformation produces compact, well-separated clusters in principal component analysis and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embeddings, achieving very high F1-scores under both One-Class Support Vector Machine and isolation forest anomaly detection methods. The proposed method exhibited robustness against broadband, narrowband, and structural noise, presenting a geometry-agnostic and computationally efficient alternative for real-time bearing diagnostics in non-stationary industrial environments.

Title: Experimental validation of a neural-network-based method for fault detection in heat pump evaporators
Authors: Lasse Jöhnk; Sebastian Borges; Leon Weingarten; Tim Klebig; Christian Vering; Dirk Müller
Abstract: The heat pump industry expects a significant shortage of qualified technicians, which will affect quick replacement and service work. It is therefore sensible to reduce unnecessary maintenance work on heat pumps. However, undetected faults can have a significant impact on efficiency and therefore, operating cost. A shift from regular maintenance to demand-based strategies is therefore desirable. Fault Detection and Diagnosis has been shown to be a valuable tool for implementing demand-based maintenance by enabling the automatic detection of malfunctions. Several methods for the automatic detection of evaporator fouling have been developed. However, experimental validation of complete fault-detection frameworks in this context remains scarce. In this study, an anomaly detection of the evaporator air volume flow is performed as a proxy for evaporator fouling. It is based on an artificial neural network that learns the behavior of the fault-free system, which is used as a reference to evaluate the current state. The residual is evaluated using a threshold-based approach and Bayesian classification in order to detect fault states. Title: A singular value decomposition and deep learning-based approach for gearbox fault detection with noisy data
Authors: Abdelhameed A. Zayed; Edric John Cruz Nacpil; Ahmed Fouly; Ali I. Siam
Abstract: Gearboxes are one of the most widely used mechanical elements in motion and power transmission. Keeping gears healthy without defects is crucial for cost-effective productivity.
