Title: A novel dynamic feature fusion method with conditional convolution and gating mechanism for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
Authors: Wentao Dong; Zanhua He; Daojin Yao; Xiaoming Wang; Jiahao Yan
Abstract: Health monitoring and fault diagnosis of rolling bearings are crucial for the continuous and effective operation of mechanical equipment. However, traditional methods often face challenges in accurately extracting fault features in complex and noisy environments, as conventional feature extraction techniques are highly susceptible to noise interference, which can result in the loss or distortion of fault information. Accordingly, a time–frequency dual-channel model based on dynamic feature fusion is proposed for fault diagnosis of bearing. The two channels employ conditional convolution (CondConv), residual connections, and Bi-LSTM to extract features from both time-domain and frequency-domain signals. CondConv dynamically generates convolutional kernels and biases, enabling the model to adaptively capture fault-specific impact features. This dynamic adjustment mechanism not only enhances the model's robustness to noise but also improves the adaptability and flexibility of feature extraction. The multi-head self-attention mechanism is adopted to capture the global correlation. Gating mechanism is introduced to dynamically regulate feature fusion, reducing redundancy and enhancing feature representation quality. Experimental results on the CWRU bearing fault dataset show that the proposed model significantly outperforms others under various noise conditions. Notably, under − 6 dB noise, the model achieved a maximum accuracy of 98.5%. Furthermore, ablation studies demonstrate that the gating mechanism plays a key role in enhancing noise resilience and classification accuracy. By dynamically optimizing the fusion of time-domain and frequency-domain features, the gating mechanism improved classification performance in noisy environments. The effectiveness of the proposed time–frequency fusion method in improving model robustness and fault diagnosis performance has been demonstrated and provides an effective reference for the accurate extraction of fault features in complex environments.

Abstract: Condition monitoring of rotating machinery is critical for ensuring industrial safety and operational reliability. As a core component of intelligent diagnostic systems, domain adaptation methods have achieved notable progress in mechanical fault diagnosis. Comprehensive experiments conducted on public and proprietary bearing datasets demonstrate that SAAN consistently surpasses state-of-the-art benchmarks in diagnostic accuracy and robustness, providing an effective solution for practical applications under class-imbalanced and variable operating conditions.

Abstract: With the increasing demand for heavy-haul railway freight, both the number and volume of heavy-haul freight cars continue to grow. The freight car braking system fault diagnosis model, which relies on historical data while failing to account for changes in braking curves when locomotives are coupled with different vehicles, is the main reason why early failures of the braking system are not diagnosed. Consequently, real-time monitoring of the freight car braking system and early fault diagnosis have emerged as a pivotal technical challenge that necessitates resolution within the framework of the railway freight maintenance reform. This paper proposes a novel hybrid-driven prediction method that effectively combines Convolutional Neural Networks, Adaptive Radial Basis Function Neural Networks, and Extreme Learning Machines (CARE). Title: Multi-Source Data Fusion and Multi-Task Physics-Informed Transformer for Power Transformer Fault Diagnosis

Experiments on 3000 samples from 76 power transformers demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high diagnostic accuracy and superior robustness under noise and interference, indicating its effectiveness for practical predictive maintenance applications.

Title: Evaluating Reconstruction-Based and Proximity-Based Methods: A Four-Way Comparison (AE, LSTM-AE, OCSVM, IF) in SCADA Anomaly Detection Under Inverted Imbalance

Abstract: This article investigates and compares four unsupervised anomaly detection algorithms: the Autoencoder (AE), LSTM-Autoencoder (LSTM-AE), One-Class SVM (OCSVM), and the Isolation Forest (IF). This performance degradation was a direct consequence of the necessity to apply a classification threshold imposed by the statistical fraction of the anomaly-dominated dataset. These results empirically demonstrate the methodological superiority of the reconstruction-based approach (AE) in constructing a stable decision boundary independent of the statistically dominant class. The study provides quantitative guidelines for the selection and calibration of algorithms in PHM diagnostic systems where states deviating from the operational norm constitute the majority.

Title: Early Anomaly Detection in Maritime Refrigerated Containers Using a Hybrid Digital Twin and Deep Learning Framework

Abstract: Maritime refrigerated containers operate under harsh and highly variable conditions, where gradual equipment degradation can lead to temperature excursions, cargo losses, and operational disruptions. In current practice, monitoring relies largely on threshold-based temperature alarms, which are reactive and provide limited insight into early abnormal behaviour. The approach is designed for shipboard constraints and uses only controller-level signals augmented by locally derived features, enabling low-complexity edge execution. The digital twin produces physically interpretable temperature residuals, while a convolutional autoencoder learns normal multivariate operating patterns and flags deviations via reconstruction error. Both indicators are integrated using conservative persistence gating to suppress short-lived transients typical of maritime operation. The framework is evaluated in a simulation environment calibrated to representative reefer thermal dynamics under variable ambient conditions and progressive fault injection across gradual and abrupt fault categories. Results indicate earlier and operationally credible detection compared to conventional alarms, supporting practical predictive maintenance in maritime cold-chain logistics.

Moreover, the framework demonstrates strong scalability, making it suitable for both individual wind turbines and large-scale wind farm systems. This research highlights the potential of quantum-inspired reinforcement learning for enabling autonomous fault tolerance and predictive maintenance in next-generation wind energy infrastructures.

Abstract: Fault detection of rotary machinery is paramount in preventing unforeseen breakdowns and providing high operational efficiency- a factor that is of great significance in any industrial setting where reliability is a crucial consideration. The core aim of the current study is to identify the robustness of SVM, kNN, and ANN models in the diagnosis of bearing defects under varying loads and speeds. At different speeds (1000 rpm, 1200 rpm, and 1400 rpm) and load conditions (4 kg, 8 kg, and 12 kg), four bearing conditions (i.e. healthy, ball defect, inner race defect, and outer race defect) have been investigated. These findings highlight the superior generalization and fault sensitivity capabilities of ANN. The results indicate how ML models, in particular ANN, can be effectively used to achieve robust and real-time condition-based monitoring and predictive maintenance of rotary systems.

Title: Model-based fault detection for an electrohydraulic braking system with cooperative regenerative braking management
Authors: Jianjian Liu; Haolun Xu; Tongqiang Luo; Yifan Yao; Wenbin Han
Abstract: This paper presents a model-based fault detection method for an electrohydraulic braking system with cooperative regenerative braking management. The regenerative braking system can save energy and improve endurance in electric vehicles. However, failure of the regenerative system may result in the system being unable to fully convert the recovered energy into stored electrical energy, with a large portion of the energy being dissipated as heat. Meanwhile, the motor braking torque output is limited, and the range of battery state of charge is affected. In this paper, a Carsim/Simulink co-simulation was developed to model the operating conditions and failure modes of the regenerative braking system in an electric vehicle. A three-stage dynamic equation was derived to model the piston movement in the wheel cylinder of the electrohydraulic braking system. A vector control using coordinate transformation was developed for the permanent magnet synchronous motor to control the current and torque. Since various system components have been built, the advantage of model-based methods can perform predictive maintenance compared with the current corrective and preventive maintenance. Title: Multi-Level Short Circuit Fault Detection in Induction Motors Using Deep CNN-LSTM Networks for Industry 4.0 Applications

Title: A Moving Window-Based Feature Extraction Method for Gearbox Fault Detection Using Vibration Signals
Authors: Ietezaz ul Hassan; Krishna Panduru; Daniel Riordan; Joseph Walsh
Abstract: Early gearbox defect detection is imperative for reducing unplanned downtime, ensuring reliability and efficiency, and minimizing maintenance expenses. This work proposes a moving window-based method for extracting statistical features from recorded vibration signals from the gearbox. The extracted features were used to train traditional ML classifiers. Moving window sizes of 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, and 800 were applied to extract statistical features from the publicly available benchmark dataset. The six different moving window sizes caused six types of datasets, each one corresponding to the moving window size. The generated datasets were partitioned using the K-fold cross-validation method to train and test ML models. This study explored and evaluated seven prominent ML classifiers: Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC), and Logistic Regression. The experimental results demonstrated that SVM, Logistic Regression, and GBC can outperform other ML classifiers. The experimental results in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall revealed that the ML classifier’s performance improves as the size of the moving window used for feature extraction increases.

Title: Uncertainty-aware multi-modal axial fan fault diagnosis: fusion of acoustic fingerprinting with transformer-BiGRU-Bayesian architecture
Authors: Zhou Li; Fanrong Wang; Xiaoran Dai; Zhongcheng Lei; Wenshan Hu; Hong Zhou
Abstract: To address the limitations of traditional single-modal diagnostic techniques and the difficulty of uncertainty quantification in deterministic models for axial fan fault diagnosis in thermal power plants, a multi-modal fault diagnosis framework integrating acoustic fingerprinting technology and a Transformer-BiGRU-Bayesian hybrid architecture is proposed. Second, a multi-modal feature fusion strategy is designed, combining F-score feature selection with nonlinear transformation to achieve deep integration of current–voltage, vibration, and acoustic features. Finally, a Transformer-BiGRU-Bayesian hybrid architecture is constructed, integrating attention mechanisms, bidirectional sequence modeling, and Mahalanobis distance-based Bayesian inference to realize fault identification and uncertainty quantification. The novelty of this work lies in the development of a non-contact acoustic fingerprinting technique for fault monitoring, the design of an effective multi-modal fusion framework that exploits complementary advantages of heterogeneous signals, and the introduction of a hybrid deep probabilistic architecture that simultaneously provides accurate diagnostics and reliable uncertainty estimation. Experiments conducted on an actual thermal power plant axial fan test platform demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 98.45%, with improvements of 3.10% to 22.48% compared to TimesNet, BiLSTM-Attention, MSCNN, Transformer-BiGRU, Transformer, BiGRU, GRU, and LSTM, respectively and Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each architectural component. In terms of uncertainty estimation, the calibration error is merely 0.23, achieving high consistency between prediction confidence and actual reliability. With increasing noise levels, the proposed model exhibits the smallest decline in diagnostic accuracy, demonstrating excellent anti-interference capability. Meanwhile, the model shows strong generalization capability across different datasets. These results indicate that the multi-modal fusion with hybrid deep probabilistic architecture significantly enhances the accuracy, reliability, and robustness of axial fan fault diagnosis in thermal power plants, providing a novel approach to equipment condition monitoring and predictive maintenance in power generation facilities.

Title: Tacholess instantaneous rotation frequency estimation and fault diagnosis base on a matching fractional synchrosqueezing transform method for wheelset bearings
Authors: Xin Li; Zengqiang Ma; Zeliang Ma; Xiaoheng Zhang
Abstract: Fault diagnosis for wheelset bearings of railway freight trains cannot rely solely on instantaneous fault frequency (IFF) extraction, but requires accurate quantification of instantaneous rotation frequency (IRF) information. Traditional tacholess methods struggle with IRF extraction due to weak signal amplitudes and significant noise interference in vibration signals. To address these challenges, a matching fractional synchrosqueezing transform (MFRSST) method is proposed. Firstly, Time-frequency ridges are extracted via peak search, with IRF curve clusters and their corresponding matching fractional orders subsequently calculated using ridge-fitting equations and bearing fault characteristic coefficients. Secondly, fractional synchrosqueezing transform (FRSST) is performed on vibration signals using matching orders derived from different assumed conditions, followed by verification of the hypotheses through time–frequency map peak values to enable tacholess IRF extraction and fault diagnosis implementation. Finally, the accuracy and noise resistance of the proposed algorithm is verified by using both simulated and measured variable speed signals. Experimental results demonstrate significant advantages: Under varying SNR simulated signals, MFRSST achieves the smallest IRF extraction error while exhibiting the strongest stability against signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) fluctuations. For actual vibration signals with single inner ring or outer ring faults, the MFRSST algorithm yields the lowest mean absolute error in IRF estimation. This represents average reductions of 92.7%, 84.3%, and 91.7% compared to MSST, TSST, and PSST, respectively. These advancements enable reliable bearing condition monitoring for freight trains, particularly beneficial for railways where tachometer installation is impractical.

The novelty lies in physics-informed integration of domain knowledge into 1D CNN framework for crucial motor fault diagnosis of variable speed drives.

Abstract: Objective To investigate the blood lead levels of lead-exposed workers in Jiangsu Province and to assess the occupational health risk in the workplace. The non-carcinogenic risk in lead-related occupations across different regions and industries were unacceptable. Conclusion Occupational health monitoring should be strengthened for male lead-exposed workers with advanced age and long service years, and electrical machinery and equipment manufacturing workers, and targeted intervention measures should be taken.

The approach offers a compact, interpretable, and data-efficient solution for early fault detection in low-speed bearings, with potential for deployment in industrial contexts where robustness and scalability are critical.

Abstract: Gears are prone to defects such as spalling, which can compromise the entire mechanical system. Effective condition monitoring is therefore essential to prevent unexpected failures. Local gear tooth defects produce transient impacts, exhibiting nonlinearity in vibration signals. Wavelet-based high order spectra (WHOS) analysis has shown promise in extracting fault-related features from such signals. However, existing methods rely on manual selection of informative bifrequency bands, limiting physical interpretability and practical applicability. To address this, an Improved Instantaneous Wavelet Bispectrum Feature (IIWBSF) for gear fault diagnostics is proposed. It incorporates a novel strategy to optimize bifrequency band selection by quantifying the fault relevance of each sub-band. The methodology is validated on both simulated signals and experimental dataset collected from a gearbox test rig at KU Leuven. The dataset comprises tests on both healthy and faulty gears (artificially induced spalling) under various speeds and loads. Vibration signals are simultaneously captured by a Wireless MEMS sensors (WMS) and a traditional piezoelectric accelerometer. Compared with the conventional approach, IIWBSF achieves superior performance in detecting faulty gear teeth and accurately identifying their quantity, angular position, and relative severity. Moreover, its consistent results on both WMS and piezoelectric accelerometer demonstrate the practical potential for industrial applications where wired accelerometer installation is constrained.

Title: Weak vibration energy powered acceleration monitoring system for bearing fault diagnosis
Authors: Zhichao Jiang; Zefang Dong; Xianpeng Fu; Zheng Gao; Likun Gong; Jie Cao; Youchao Qi; Tingshan Liu; Wei Li; Chi Zhang
Abstract: Vibration monitoring technology has been widely applied in industrial, transportation, and other environments. Traditional wired and battery-powered methods face challenges such as complex wiring, high energy consumption, and environmental pollution. Here, we have developed a self-powered wireless acceleration monitoring system (SWAMS) for monitoring the operating condition of bearings in a weak vibration environment. A vibration triboelectric nanogenerator array (WEB-TENGs) is designed to efficiently harvest energy from micro-amplitude vibration, and supplies power to SWAMS. The WEB-TENGs achieves a notable peak power density of 4.3 μW/cm<sup>3</sup> under an acceleration of 0.07 g (10 µm excitation amplitude at 42.1 Hz). The WEB-TENGs can efficiently charge lithium batteries by a power management module. The SWAMS can transmit vibration data within each hour without additional power consumption, using a timing circuit module. The collected acceleration data from the bearing housing is wirelessly transmitted to a PC via a transmission module. Fault identification of bearings is performed using a hybrid CNN-LSTM model, achieving a classification accuracy of 98 % on the test set. The SWAMS enables self-powered vibration monitoring of industrial equipment in unattended environments, providing a sustainable and maintenance-free solution for fault diagnosis.

Title: Enhancing machine learning classifier performance in bearing fault diagnosis through feature-based ranking
Authors: Abdul Khaliq Ansari; Paras Kumar
Abstract: The condition monitoring and problem identification of tapered roller bearings (TRBs) is a critical and laborious process. Its main goal is to evaluate the important parts of equipment and systems for health. The state of these components is considered while making maintenance choices during actual operations. Using innovative techniques to automate fault diagnosis reduces the need for experienced individuals. The selection of high-ranking features enhances the accuracy of fault detection. Understanding the impact of various feature ranking algorithms on the efficiency of Machine Learning in detecting bearing defects is very important. Method: This work presents a study on the influence of feature-based ranking for condition monitoring and fault diagnosis on ML classifiers. For this customised test rig data and one open-source MFPT (Machinery Failure Prevention Technology) dataset are employed. Result: The selection of unique features via feature ranking greatly impacts the efficiency of machine learning models. The highest accuracy in defect classification is attained using the best 10 best features identified by the KW test across all SVM kernels. Classification accuracies obtained for linear, quadratic, cubic, fine, medium, and coarse models are 79.0%, 86.6%, 92.9%, 97.6%, 81.9%, and 64.4%, respectively for tapered bearing dataset. Similar trend obtained from MFPT dataset giving corresponding accuracies are 86.7%, 95.8%, 99.7%, 100%, 88.8% and 65.0%. The Kruskal–Wallis (KW) test surpasses the One-way ANOVA (Ow-A) in all cases for both datasets.

Title: Speed-guided diffusion probabilistic model integrated with variational autoencoder for fault diagnosis under limited data
Authors: Xuemei Liu; Kai Zhou; Min Xia; Chunsheng Yang; Yuejian Chen
Abstract: Deep learning-based fault diagnosis has shown great potential in intelligent condition monitoring. However, its performance heavily depends on large amounts of labeled data, which are often scarce in real-world industrial scenarios, especially under varying speed conditions. The data limitations hinder the generalization ability of fault diagnosis models. To address this issue, we propose a novel speed-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model integrated with variational autoencoder (SDPM-VAE) for generating high quality data. The speed signal is incorporated as a conditional prior through a cross-attention mechanism to preserve speed-dependent characteristics in the generated data. Additionally, a hybrid VAE and DDPM framework is proposed to enhance data quality while reducing computational cost. The coarse reconstructions and latent representations derived from the VAE are integrated into the reverse diffusion process. Experimental results on two gearbox datasets demonstrate that the SDPM-VAE outperforms four state-of-the-art methods in both the quality of the generated data and fault diagnosis accuracy, thereby validating its effectiveness for data augmentation under limited data conditions.

Title: Temporal-enhanced transformer for anomaly detection in spacecraft irregular-interval telemetry
Authors: Aixin Dai; Yancai Xiao; Fangyi Ren; Haikuo Shen; Shaodan Zhi; Biao Ma
Abstract: Ensuring operational safety through spacecraft health monitoring critically relies on effective anomaly detection. However, the task is significantly complicated by irregular time intervals in real-world telemetry data. To address this pressing issue, we propose TETAD, a novel end-to-end Temporal-Enhanced Transformer model specifically designed for such data. TETAD integrates a unique Temporal-Enhanced Transformer (TET) architecture featuring our key innovation: the Temporal Enhancement Encoding Module (TEEM). TEEM effectively captures complex irregular-interval temporal features by encoding time interval information alongside learnable positional embeddings. Furthermore, a contrastive learning strategy boosts the model’s discriminative capability between normal and anomalous patterns. Evaluated extensively on real-world spacecraft telemetry and public datasets, TETAD demonstrates substantial improvements in anomaly detection precision and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods. Extensive experimental analysis validates the effectiveness of our proposed mechanisms and the overall advantages of TETAD. Our work provides a robust and practical solution for enhancing spacecraft health monitoring reliability and introduces a novel deep architecture for sophisticated temporal feature extraction.

Title: Research on the Teaching Reform of the Equipment Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis Course
Authors: Yi Yang; Lun Zhang; Yanhong Zhu; Niaoqing Hu; Guoji Shen; Zhe Cheng
Abstract: This study proposes a research-oriented teaching reform framework in response to critical challenges in the Equipment Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis course, including disconnection from engineering practice, excessively broad content coverage, students' weak foundational knowledge, and insufficient research-task-driven learning. With the development of intelligent electromechanical equipment, this course is crucial for cultivating fault diagnosis talents urgently needed by enterprises. However, the involvement of multidisciplinary knowledge leads to high teaching difficulty and low student learning enthusiasm. To address this contradiction, this study takes the integration of teaching and research as a breakthrough point: firstly, streamline the teaching content, focus on the core knowledge of rotating machinery fault diagnosis, and introduce the latest achievements of the teacher research team; Secondly, construct a student-centered classroom, strengthen proactive exploration and teamwork abilities through group research tasks, literature research, and final flipped classroom presentations; Finally, by deeply integrating engineering practice and removing redundant theories, typical cases (such as fan and compressor fault diagnosis) and project driven teaching are used to cultivate students' analytical abilities, and students are required to complete research reports and presentations. The reform aims to enable students to independently construct knowledge systems, enhance learning enthusiasm, engineering cognition, and innovation ability through project driven, research environment creation, and engineering ability training, and provide a scalable teaching path for mechanical related professional courses.

Title: Optical fiber sensing and partial discharge fault diagnosis for power cable health monitoring
Authors: Haoyuan Tian; Ruimin Song; Jinchao Du; Jianxin Wang; Hong Liu; Weikai Zhang; Yuxuan Song; Zhixian Zhang; Weigen Chen
Abstract: Partial discharge (PD) in power cables is a significant precursor to cable insulation aging and failure. Accurately monitoring PD is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of power systems. This paper proposes a method for detecting PD in power cables based on a fiber-optic Michelson interferometer. This method leverages the high sensitivity and electromagnetic interference resistance of the fiber-optic Michelson interferometer to achieve real-time detection of acoustic signals generated by PD in cables. To address the noise interference present during the detection process, this paper designs an effective noise reduction algorithm to improve the signal-to-noise ratio. Subsequently, time-frequency (TF) analysis techniques are used to extract features from the de-noised signal. The resulting TF images are then used as a training dataset for a deep learning model, enabling automatic recognition and classification of PD signals. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy of PD detection, validating the potential application of a fiber-optic Michelson interferometer combined with signal processing and deep learning techniques in monitoring PD in power cables.

Title: Light Weight Decision Tree-Based Onboard Fault Diagnostic for Stator Winding Severity Evaluation

Abstract: Detecting and diagnosing faults in industrial systems is important for ensuring their reliable operation. The approach uses a DT-based model to extract relevant features and adapt them to specific faults. Additionally, it investigates the severity of stator winding insulation failures by combining deep learning with time–frequency-based features. This work demonstrates the reliability and scalability of the model, making it suitable for industrial applications.

Title: Two-Stage Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Cross-Domain Anomaly Detection and Failure Prediction
Authors: Rahomotul Islam; Nafiza Humauara Hasan Neha; Mumtahina Ahmed; Jannatul Maua; Neha Chaudhary; M. F. Mridha; Nilanjan Dey; Satyabrata Roy
Abstract: Industrial systems require effective anomaly detection and predictive maintenance strategies to prevent unexpected failures and optimize operational efficiency. However, traditional approaches often treat anomaly detection and failure prediction as independent tasks, limiting their ability to leverage operational patterns for early fault diagnosis. This article proposes a novel two-stage hybrid deep learning framework that integrates unsupervised anomaly detection with supervised failure prediction through cross-domain transfer learning. The framework first employs a variational autoencoder (VAE) to extract latent anomaly embeddings from HVAC system operational data without requiring labeled anomalies. These embeddings are transferred and combined with sensor readings from a predictive maintenance dataset to enrich the failure prediction model. Experimental evaluations on two publicly available datasets demonstrate that the proposed hybrid model achieves superior performance compared to conventional methods, with notable improvements in accuracy (90.2%), precision (0.89), recall (0.90), F1-score (0.90), and AUC-ROC (0.873). Additionally, the approach exhibits strong cross-domain generalization ability, highlighting its potential applicability across different industrial environments. This work introduces a scalable and flexible anomaly-driven transfer learning strategy that addresses the scarcity of labeled failure data and enhances the robustness of predictive maintenance systems. The findings suggest that integrating unsupervised operational insights into supervised learning frameworks is a promising direction for advancing intelligent industrial monitoring.

Title: INTELLIGENT FAULT DIAGNOSIS OF ELECTROMECHANICAL EQUIPMENT BASED ON IOT AND DEEP LEARNING
Authors: Xiali Yue
Abstract: Fault diagnosis of electromechanical equipment plays an important role in ensuring the reliability and safety of industrial systems. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle to capture complex nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional data, especially under imbalanced conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid framework that combines artificial neural network (ANN)-based feature extraction with ensemble machine learning models for fault diagnosis. First, an ANN is employed to learn high-level representations from the original input features. The extracted features are then fed into multiple machine learning models, including random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), and k-nearest neighbors (KNN), to perform classification. To further improve performance, the best-performing models are selected and combined using a logistic regression-based adaptive weighting strategy. In addition, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied to alleviate the class imbalance problem. Experimental results conducted on the publicly available AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset, which is a synthetic dataset designed to simulate industrial electromechanical equipment operating conditions, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance compared with individual models. In particular, the ensemble model (ANN+RF+KNN) achieves the best results in terms of F1-score, indicating a better balance between precision and recall. The findings show that combining deep feature learning with ensemble strategies can significantly enhance fault diagnosis performance.

Abstract: In recent days, predictive maintenance is a major component in modern industrial systems, which minimizes downtime and operational costs by enabling early detection of equipment anomalies. Title: Feature Disentanglement Augmented Network for Vibration-Based Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery Under Unknown Operating Conditions
Authors: Yixuan Shan; Peixuan Ding; Xilian Yang; Chen Wang; Zhongyang Fei
Abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis of rotating machinery based on vibration measurements is essential for reliable condition monitoring and predictive maintenance in industrial systems. However, conventional data-driven diagnostic models often experience significant performance degradation under varying operating conditions, primarily due to distribution shifts in the acquired vibration signals. This article proposes a feature disentanglement augmented network (FDAN) to improve the robustness and generalization capability of vibration-based fault diagnosis for rotating machinery to unseen target domains. In FDAN, a disentanglement network is employed to explicitly separate the input features into domain-invariant and domain-specific components. An independently trained attention module is further introduced to identify the most classification-relevant components, which are subsequently used for augmentation to enrich the diversity of the learned representations. The proposed method requires no test-condition data during training, making it well-suited for industrial scenarios. Extensive experiments conducted on the widely used DIRG and SDUST fault datasets demonstrate that FDAN consistently outperforms several domain generalization (DG) approaches, achieving significant improvements in diagnostic accuracy under varying working conditions. Additional validations, including feature analysis and ablation studies, confirm the effectiveness and necessity of each component. These results demonstrate the potential of FDAN as an effective and deployable solution for robust intelligent fault diagnosis in vibration measurement-based monitoring of rotating machinery in industrial applications.

Title: A Collaborative Denoising and Multi-Sensor Local-Global Fusion Framework for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery Under Noisy Environments
Authors: Shijie Lu; Binbin Qin; Qinghua Zhang; Yongqi Qiu; Guoxi Sun
Abstract: Accurate measurement and fault diagnosis of rotating machinery are paramount for the safe and reliable monitoring of modern industrial systems. In practical sensing applications, however, accurate state detection is severely challenged by strong background noise and the complexity of physical fault signatures, especially concerning the effective processing and fusion of multi-sensor measurement data. To tackle this industrial measurement and monitoring challenge, we propose a novel measurement data processing method, named Collaborative Denoising and Multi-sensor Local-Global Fusion Framework (CDMSLGFF). At its core, the proposed method introduces an innovative dual-branch feature extractor to effectively characterize the mechanical condition: one branch performs deep feature denoising and extracts local physical details from sensor readings via a multi-scale refinement denoising module (MRDM), while the other captures global contextual dependencies of the measurement data using a discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and a Transformer architecture. This differential design ensures synergistic noise suppression and complementary feature extraction from multiple sensing perspectives. Subsequently, a hierarchical adaptive fusion module (HAFM) is proposed to intelligently screen, enhance, and reconstruct characteristics from both branches, generating a robust fused representation with high discriminability and noise invariance. Extensive experiments on real-world industrial (RWI) and public measurement datasets demonstrate that the proposed method provides a novel and superior monitoring and detection solution, significantly advancing multi-sensor information fusion and fault diagnosis reliability in harsh measurement environments.

Title: Robust energy centric machine learning assisted fault detection & diagnosis: an extrusion case
Authors: Corentin Ferreira; Kevin N. Otto; Wen Li; Tansu Alpcan; Boris Eisenbart
Abstract: Condition monitoring for fault detection and diagnosis in industrial systems typically relies on vibration, temperature, or pressure signals, with machine learning playing an increasingly crucial role. Yet, its potential remains under-explored, with past decade works focusing mainly on fault detection. In this study, we propose an improved energy-centric condition monitoring framework for fault detection and isolation. Since energy is a single aggregated system-wide variable, we emphasise the importance of feature engineering to extract discriminative fault signatures. Our approach was evaluated on a plastic extrusion system under seven fault conditions and only system-wide energy measurements and timestamps were used for fault detection, isolation and robustness analysis. We use deep unsupervised models, specifically autoencoders and variational autoencoders, trained on engineered features to detect deviations from normal behaviour and isolate fault types. Moreover, the models showed robust performance under measurement noise arising from adjacent machinery or unmonitored operational variables, maintaining high detection accuracy even with 20% additive noise, where conventional models dropped below 60%. Robustness to sensor drift was also evaluated. Isolation scores remained high when detection was achieved with our models. These findings demonstrate that energy-based monitoring, when properly engineered, can be a cost-effective, robust alternative for industrial condition monitoring.

Title: A simulation-to-reality transfer learning method based on Kolmogorov-Arnold network enhanced model for bearing fault diagnosis
Authors: Qibin Wang; Dinglong Zheng; Chenyi Lin; Jiacheng Wei; Yi Wang; Jiaqi Ye
Abstract: Efficient fault diagnosis for rotating machinery is crucial, but in practical engineering, obtaining fault data is difficult due to high costs and significant risks. Meanwhile, although simulation can generate data, model simplification leads to a significant discrepancy with real signals, making direct application challenging. Therefore, a simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) transfer learning method based on Kolmogorov-Arnold network enhanced model for bearing fault diagnosis is proposed. Title: RT-AD: Real-Time Anomaly Detection of Time-Series Data Based on Lightweight Periodic Transformers for Industrial Edge Devices

Title: Robust Deep Learning Models for Fault Detection in Grid-tied Solar Inverters: A Comparative Study of LSTM, Bi-LSTM, and CNN-LSTM Architectures
Authors: Darshan Pankajkumar Patel; Ishan Prashant Pathak; Dawson Roach; Nuri Yilmazer
Abstract: Grid-tied solar inverters, which are essential for renewable energy integration, represent the most failure-prone components in photovoltaic systems, with failure rates reaching 28% of total system failures. Rapid fault detection can not only save components but also ensure grid stability. However, in real-world operating conditions, such as noise, variable loads, and non-linear dynamics, conventional detection approaches are challenged. Unlike existing simulation-based studies, there is a critical gap in hardware-validated, real-time fault detection approaches under realistic noise conditions. This study evaluates and compares three advanced deep learning architectures, LSTM, Bi-LSTM, and a hybrid 1D CNN-LSTM for multi-class fault classification in grid-connected solar inverters. The models were trained and tested using time-series datasets generated through OPAL-RT simulation with Raspberry Pi 4 under diverse fault scenarios with added sensor noise to simulate realistic environments of grid-tied solar inverters. The Bi-LSTM provided superior temporal context learning, whereas the CNN-LSTM excelled in feature extraction from complex fault signatures. The results show CNN-LSTM as a strong candidate for real-time, noise-resilient fault detection in renewable energy systems, clearing the path for intelligent inverter monitoring solutions.

Title: AFIAN: An Open-set Cross-domain Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Method based on Multi-modal Signals
Authors: Yongze Jin; Mengyang Li; Nan Feng; Junqi Liu; Xiaohao Song; Wenjiang Ji; Xinhong Hei
Abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) is widely recognized as a cornerstone technology for ensuring the safety and reliability of modern industrial systems. In real-world engineering applications, however, the diagnostic performance of IFD systems is degraded by varying operating conditions and the emergence of previously unseen faults, which can lead to unreliable decisions and reduced maintenance effectiveness. Extensive experiments conducted on three types of mechanical equipment under diverse operating conditions demonstrate that AFIAN significantly improves diagnostic robustness, open-set recognition capability, and cross-domain generalization performance. These results indicate that the proposed method has strong potential for practical deployment in industrial health monitoring systems, especially in complex scenarios involving variable conditions, multi-sensor data, and unknown fault patterns.

Title: ST-DATNet: Spectro-Temporal Domain-Adaptive Transfer Network with Feature-Based Alignment for Cross-Domain Engine Fault Diagnosis
Authors: Heteng Zhang
Abstract: Engine fault diagnosis plays a pivotal role in predictive maintenance for industrial systems, yet traditional supervised learning approaches suffer from severe performance degradation when deployed across different equipment or operating conditions due to distribution shift. Existing methods face three critical limitations: (1) they fail to capture the spectrotemporal characteristics of mechanical vibration signals that encode fault-specific frequency patterns and transient signatures, (2) conventional transfer learning techniques indiscriminately align source and target domains without considering sample-level transferability, leading to negative transfer and collapsed class boundaries, and (3) domain adaptation mechanisms often overlook the importance of preserving fault-discriminative features while achieving distribution alignment, resulting in reduced diagnostic accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose ST-DATNet (Spectro-Temporal Domain-Adaptive Transfer Network), an end-to-end neural framework for crossdomain engine fault diagnosis. Our approach introduces three key innovations corresponding to the identified limitations: (1) a spectro-temporal encoder utilizing Short-Time Fourier Transform to jointly model frequency-domain harmonic structures and timedomain degradation dynamics, (2) a transferability-weighted knowledge transfer mechanism that assigns higher importance to source samples geometrically proximate to the target distribution while enforcing class-conditional alignment to maintain fault boundaries, and (3) a hybrid domain adaptation module integrating adversarial learning and Maximum Mean Discrepancy minimization to learn representations that are simultaneously domain-invariant and fault-discriminative. Extensive experiments on the Engine Fault Detection Dataset validate ST-DATNet's superiority, achieving 97.45% accuracy and 99.12% AUC while outperforming 16 state-of-the-art baselines by substantial margins. SHAP-based interpretability analysis further confirms that our model correctly identifies mechanically meaningful featuresvibrations for early warnings and thermal anomalies for critical failures.

Title: EWSNet: Physics-Informed Wavelet Initialization and Balanced Dynamic Adaptive Thresholding for Noise-Robust Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis under Severe Vibration Noise Interference
Authors: Feihang Wang; Xiaoyu Wang; Xiaojia Wang
Abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings based on vibration signal analysis has become a cornerstone of predictive maintenance in modern industrial systems. Despite remarkable advances in deep learning-based approaches, three critical challenges remain underexplored: (1) conventional random weight initialization strategies disregard the oscillatory and transient physics inherent in vibration signals, resulting in slow convergence and limited interpretability; (2) existing denoising mechanisms rely on fixed or purely data-driven thresholds that fail to adaptively balance noise suppression and fault feature preservation under varying vibration noise intensities; (3) single-pathway feature extraction architectures cannot simultaneously capture multi-scale temporal patterns spanning global waveform morphology and localized transient impulses. To address these limitations, we propose EWSNet, a novel deep tri-stream network that integrates three synergistic innovations: (1) an enhanced Laplace wavelet basis with a scale smoothing factor for physics-informed convolutional weight initialization, embedding domain-specific vibration priors into the network; (2) a balanced dynamic adaptive threshold module that learns an optimal interpolation between soft and hard thresholding through a trainable balancing parameter, achieving robust denoising under severe vibration noise contamination; (3) a tristream feature fusion architecture that extracts coarse-grained, fine-grained, and denoised representations in parallel. Extensive experiments on the CWRU bearing dataset demonstrate that EWSNet achieves 99.87% accuracy under clean conditions and maintains 99.08% accuracy even at SNR =-4 dB, substantially outperforming eight state-of-the-art methods.

Title: Integrating Fault Diagnosis Into Prognostics for Fuzzy Stochastic Distribution Control Systems: An Optimization-Based Online Approach
Authors: Youxuan Gao; Lina Yao; Shuiwang Yuan; Shenze Chen
Abstract: Detailed degradation information can help uncover the underlying mechanisms of system degradation and provide essential guidance for accurate prognostics. However, obtaining such information in practice is often costly and challenging, which has motivated the development of prognostics methods that integrate fault diagnosis. Most existing methods, however, primarily focus on degradation magnitude while neglecting trend information, and they also lack sufficient robustness to uncertainties. As a result, they often suffer from low prediction accuracy and limited prediction horizons. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel diagnosis-integrated prognostics framework in which the remaining useful life prediction task is formulated as an explicit parameter optimization problem. Specifically, the robustness of optimization algorithms contributes to reliable prediction accuracy even under imprecise prior knowledge and low-quality data, while the integration of degradation trend information enhances the ability to capture long-term dynamics, which in turn extends the prediction horizon. To better reflect realistic operating conditions, concurrent actuator and sensor faults are considered. The approach first extracts both magnitude and trend information via fault diagnosis, and then employs parameter optimization for RUL prediction. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulation studies of actuator and sensor degradation in a grain processing system. Note to Practitioners—Fault prognostics is a key component of predictive maintenance, as it enables the prevention of catastrophic failures and reduces losses associated with maintenance downtime. The motivation of this study lies in achieving more accurate and reliable online fault prognostics. To this end, this paper introduces fault diagnosis techniques into the prognostic process, leveraging diagnostic information to enhance prediction accuracy and stability. From a practical engineering perspective, the proposed method offers high implementability and low deployment cost, as it requires almost no additional information beyond that obtained from fault diagnosis, thereby reducing implementation difficulty. Moreover, it can be seamlessly integrated into existing diagnostic modules of industrial systems without the need to modify or redeploy the current diagnostic framework, which simplifies system integration and further lowers implementation cost.

Title: Sensorless-Based Anomaly Detection and Degradation Assessment of Roller Chain Systems
Authors: J. Qi; Y. Uhlmann; Z. Chen; G. Schullerus
Abstract: The reliability of mechanical systems in industrial applications profoundly impacts the overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), encompassing quality, efficiency, and operational costs. In the past, much research on CM has focused on bearings and gears, while other types of rotating machinery, such as chain systems, have received comparatively less attention. These systems are widely employed across various applications including conveyor systems, packaging machinery, and power transmission in mobility, agriculture, mining, and production machinery. This work addresses these industrial challenges by introducing an innovative approach utilizing sensorless strategies and motor information-facilitated process data for CM in roller chain systems. Our methodology offers several distinct advantages: (1) We employ a sensorless strategy, utilizing readily available motor-driver-read process data, to eliminate the need for complex sensor selection, installation, and data management. This approach enhances cost-effectiveness and applicability across diverse industrial systems. (2) By leveraging process data from the motor controller, we segment data and integrate data fusion techniques, to provide a comprehensive understanding of the system’s behavior, which enables the improvement of the CM performance. (3) We compare various features for degradation assessment and implement anomaly detection based on k-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithms, effectively identifying abnormal statuses in roller chains. Through the validation, the developed methodology demonstrates its effectiveness in addressing real-world CM challenges in industrial environments, offering a cost-effective and reliable solution.

Title: Construction of an Equipment Risk Anomaly Detection Model Enabled by Machine Learning Algorithms

Abstract: This study proposes a two-stage hybrid learning framework that integrates Isolation Forest (iForest) and Random Forest (RF) to jointly address anomaly detection and risk classification in sensor-based industrial systems. Subsequently, a Random Forest classifier is trained using six engineered features - including anomaly duration and the number of concurrently triggered sensors - alongside a domain-knowledge-informed pseudo-labeling rule to distinguish risky anomalies from non-risky ones. Evaluation on the test set achieves an overall accuracy of 98.33%, with a precision of 100% and a recall of 75% specifically for risky anomalies. Feature importance analysis reveals that duration and the number of affected sensors collectively account for 75.66% of the model' s discriminative power. The performance remained stable when the noise level did not exceed 5%, and the accuracy rate remained above 98% even when the feature missing rate reached 40%.The proposed framework demonstrates both strong interpretability and robustness in unlabeled,real-world industrial settings - offering a practical and reliable methodological foundation for predictive maintenance,real-time equipment monitoring, and early-warning systems.

Title: TRACE: Time series representation learning with contrastive embeddings for anomaly detection in photovoltaic systems
Authors: Chandana Priya Nivarthi; Zhixin Huang; Christian Gruhl; Bernhard Sick
Abstract: Reliable anomaly detection in photovoltaic (PV) inverters is critical for ensuring operational efficiency and reducing maintenance costs in renewable energy systems. We introduce TRACE (Time series Representation learning with Autoencoder-based Contrastive Embeddings), a self-supervised contrastive learning framework for multivariate time series anomaly detection in PV systems. TRACE employs a two-stage architecture: autoencoder-based representation learning with interchangeable backbones followed by contrastive training through a Siamese network. The framework generates semantically coherent augmentations by perturbing autoencoder reconstructions and applies three negative mining strategies to create challenging contrastive pairs. Comprehensive experiments on a real-world PV inverter dataset and two industrial benchmarks demonstrate TRACE's superiority. Autoencoder-based augmentations deliver a 21.3% relative improvement in mean F1 (0.616 vs. 0.508) over traditional perturbation methods, with TransformerAE emerging as the optimal backbone architecture. While negative sampling strategies show dataset-specific advantages, their impact remains secondary to encoder capacity. TRACE with TransformerAE and reconstruction-error negatives consistently outperforms fourteen state-of-the-art time series anomaly detection methods, achieving highest F1 scores on all the three datasets while maintaining exceptional precision up to 0.99. Visualization analysis confirms TRACE's capacity for early fault detection up to three days before failure and interpretable embedding separation. The framework addresses the fundamental challenge of label scarcity in industrial monitoring through self-supervised learning, providing a practical and transparent solution for predictive maintenance in PV systems and broader industrial applications.

Title: Adaptive Multimodal Industrial Fault Diagnosis with Attention-Driven Fusion Boosting Unimodal Performance
Authors: Di Wang; Xinyu Pan; Yuanyuan Gao; Fugee Tsung; Fangyu Li
Abstract: Industrial fault diagnosis increasingly benefits from Large Models (LMs), which can handle diverse data sources. Within this context, multimodal approaches, which integrate inputs like vibration, process, and video data, boost accuracy but often assume all modalities are available, which rarely holds in practice due to sensor failures, deployment limits, etc. While unimodal methods are more practical, they often lack sufficient information for complex scenarios. The key challenge is how to effectively fuse multimodal data and transfer that knowledge to enhance unimodal performance when some modalities are missing. This paper proposes an adaptive multimodal fault diagnosis framework that enables bidirectional enhancement between multimodal and unimodal representations. For model construction, a Cross-Fusion Channel Attention (CFCA) module is introduced to align features across modalities, and then a Shared Temporal Attention (STA) module captures sequential dependencies and facilitates representation sharing. A multi-head diagnosis structure is finally used to jointly supervise both multimodal and unimodal branches. For parameter estimation, we develop a similarity-aware and uncertainty-guided gradient modulation strategy to adaptively balance multimodal and unimodal learning, ensuring stable optimization and knowledge transfer. Experiments on the real-world industrial PRONTO dataset demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance and adaptability across various scenarios with varying modality availability. Note to Practitioners - This paper provides a practical method for fault diagnosis based on multimodal data of industrial systems, including manufacturing, rotating machinery, and process plants. In this setting, multiple sensor modalities are required to jointly monitor the same complex process or object, and samples are constructed according to the proposed hybrid alignment strategy. For model construction, practitioners first use modality-specific encoders to process data of each modality independently. Subsequently, the model structure includes two key components: a CFCA module for feature alignment, and an STA module for temporal modeling, followed by a multi-head classifier for flexible inference. To train the model, practitioners implement the adaptive gradient modulation strategy that integrates multimodal and unimodal supervision by considering both gradient similarity and uncertainty. The proposed method is modularly designed and interoperable with legacy systems, and thus well-suited for implementing predictive maintenance across diverse operational settings.

Title: Transformer with Self Attention Mechanism for Electric Motor Fault Detection
Authors: Ashish Kumar Sinha; Prince; Prashant Kumar
Abstract: Reliable fault detection in electric motors is essential in ensuring operational safety, minimizing downtime, and lowering maintenance costs in modern industrial systems. The proposed methodology enables efficient feature learning without relying on handcrafted features or recurrent neural networks. This is done by directly modeling temporal correlations within multi-sensor motor signals using the Transformer architecture. Under different operating settings, the self-attention mechanism improves sensitivity to subtle fault characteristics by adaptively highlighting signal segments that are relevant to the defect. These findings demonstrate that attention-based transformer designs provide a potent and scalable solution for sophisticated electric motor status monitoring and problem detection.

Title: A Dual-Scheme Cointegration Framework for Condition Monitoring and Fault Detection Using Non-Joint and Mixed-Order Time Series
Authors: Nasir H.R. Syed; Debela A. Teklemariyem; Wieslaw J. Staszewski; Phong B. Dao
Abstract: Recent years have seen growing faith in data-driven tools for condition monitoring and fault detection, a trend accelerated further by advances in artificial intelligence. In many industrial systems typical examples like chemical plants and wind-energy installations-the underlying process variables do not behave in a stable or predictable manner. Their statistical features shift over time, and conventional monitoring methods which assume an essentially stationary assumption, often struggle to handle high-dimensional signals. Much of the difficulty stems from the fact that several variables move together over long periods but differ in their degree of non-stationarity. To deal with this challenge, two monitoring strategies are designed to react reliably to deviations even when the data show complicated stochastic behaviour. The framework consists of two cointegration-based schemes. Scheme 1 treats all series jointly (i.e., mixed order), regardless of their integration order, while Scheme 2, first separates them into (0), (1), and (2) groups using the augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test and then each group fed to cointegration model individually. In both cases, the residuals serve as indicators. Monitoring statistics are estimated based on the Mahalanobis Distance (MD), utilizing residuals from testing set; the control limit (CL) is computed based on the Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) utilizing residuals from training set. Any deviation of monitoring statistics crossing the CL highlights the abnormal conditions in the system. Numerical case studies demonstrate the efficacy of non-joint cointegration-based monitoring (Scheme 2), which provides a flexible and computationally efficient method for monitoring non-stationary processes. In comparison to traditional PCA and CA-based Schemes, the Scheme 2 framework has better performance with a lower false alarm.

Title: KFD-AEEScan: a Katz fractal dimension acoustic emission event scanner for single-sensor multi-fault diagnosis in milling machines
Authors: Andrei Maliuk; Tuan Khai Nguyen; Zahoor Ahmad; Jong Myon Kim
Abstract: Reliable condition monitoring of milling machines (MMs) is essential for maintaining quality of the output product and avoiding downtime, but traditional acoustic emission (AE)-based approaches using features such as root mean square (RMS), kurtosis, or band-limited energies either blur burst events with background activity or rely on ad hoc thresholding of AE hits. As a result, rotation-synchronous AE bursts generated by tool wear, bearing damage, and gear defects are incompletely captured and difficult to exploit for robust multi-fault diagnosis. This article presents Katz fractal dimension AE event scanner (KFD-AEEScan), a single-sensor diagnostic framework that processes AE signals into time-scale maps of local fractal complexity, replacing purely amplitude- or energy-based traces with a multiscale representation more sensitive to transient burst activity. A sliding-window Katz fractal-dimension estimator is applied at multiple window lengths, producing KFD traces in which burst-dominated regions gravitate toward the lower bound of KFD, while quasi-stationary background occupies higher-complexity levels. These traces are synchronized and stacked into compact two-dimensional time-scale maps, in which multiple KFD scales jointly encode the prominence and timing of AE bursts along each cutting pass. The framework is validated on real milling-machine AE data under multiple spindle speeds and four health states: normal, cutting tool wear, spindle bearing fault, and gearbox fault. KFD-AEEScan achieves high, well-balanced macro-F1 across all classes and outperforms representative wavelet-fractal, short-time Fourier transform-based, and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD)-fractal baselines. The results indicate that localized KFD mapping of AE bursts provides an effective representation for multi-fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance in MMs.

Title: Digital Twin-Driven Fault Diagnosis for Aircraft Hydraulic Systems: A Multi-Sensor Data Fusion Approach with Real-Time Anomaly Detection

These results demonstrate that the proposed RBF-ANN framework provides an accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient solution for real-time wind turbine fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance.

Furthermore, the variability of the training dataset is identified as a key factor influencing out-of-distribution generalization performance. The findings demonstrate the generalizability of autoencoder based monitoring approaches across different cutting conditions and provide insights for data-driven and grey-box modeling frameworks in manufacturing.

Abstract: It is necessary to inspect the health of the lithium-ion batteries to make them work efficiently and last longer in energy storage devices. With complex changes over time and space, it might prove hard to achieve accurate estimates. This paper introduces a new Deep Kernel Gaussian Process (DKGP) approach that merges offline Gaussian processes with real-time spatiotemporal analysis through a novel deep kernel design. The new approach outperforms previous techniques by integrating two forms of Gaussian processes and a deep kernel design to capture complex features and efficiently analyze spatiotemporal data. The DKGP is unique in that it employs deep neural networks to learn the kernel and adaptive Gaussian processes to quantify uncertainty, enhancing prediction accuracy and confidence. Experiments on a high-fidelity dataset consisting of 29 pairs of 24 V lithium iron phosphate battery systems comprising 232 individual batteries and more than 131 million operation records demonstrate outstanding results with 0.038 RMSE and 0.027 MAE, along with stable predictions in a 95% confidence interval. The DKGP performs excellently in discovering wear patterns in batteries and keeping them operational across varied conditions. Compared to conventional single-modal techniques, the technique performs better in the time-space analysis, and the deep kernel design provides higher reliability and adaptability. The advantages of improved tracking of the health of the batteries include precision, stability, and usability across many industries. Future research will involve enhancing calculations and designing transfer learning mechanisms for various applications.

Title: Benchmarking Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Multiclass Wind Turbine Fault Diagnosis Using SCADA Data
Authors: Anshu Kumar; Ankit Rattan; Ankita Yadav; Aakash Sinha; Sachin Singh
Abstract: In this work, we compare and evaluate different deep learning and machine learning approaches for multiclass fault diagnosis in wind turbine systems using SCADA data. A pipeline is implemented including feature filtering, normalization, and sliding-window sequence generation. Multiple models are evaluated, including recurrent networks, convolutional and hybrid architectures, TCN (Temporal Convolutional Networks), Transformer-based models, and an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) baseline model. Experimental results show that models with temporal attention and convolutional feature extraction have better performance than traditional recurrent architectures in capturing complex SCADA patterns. The study highlights the importance of realistic benchmarking and offers practical insights into selecting a suitable model for SCADA-based wind turbine condition monitoring.

Title: Artificial neural network and acoustic emission-based fault diagnosis for wide temperature range silicon carbide MOSFET application
Authors: Ruby Beniwal; Shruti Kalra
Abstract: This study presents a dual-domain diagnostic framework combining acoustic emission (AE) sensing and artificial neural network (ANN) modeling for real-time fault detection in silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs operating from 25 <sup>∘</sup>C to 500 <sup>∘</sup>C. Gate-source overvoltage-induced stress waves were analyzed across three MOSFET types, with IRFP150NPBF exhibiting a 3.2× rise in peak-to-peak amplitude beyond 80 V. An ANN trained using segmented Latin hypercube sampling (SLHS) achieved 17.3% improved accuracy over standard LHS in I-V characteristic prediction. To evaluate real-world consistency, the ANN-predicted characteristics were benchmarked against experimental and datasheet data from commercial SiC MOSFETs (Wolfspeed C3M0065090J and ROHM SCT3060AL), showing ⩽ 7% deviation in drain current and ⩽ 8% deviation in transconductance across 25<sup>∘</sup>C-500 <sup>∘</sup>C. The integrated AE-ANN approach thus enables low-rate sampling, rapid convergence, and non-invasive diagnostics validated against empirical datasets, enhancing reliability modeling and predictive maintenance for high-temperature power electronics.

Title: Intelligent fault diagnosis algorithm for Lithium-ion batteries based on hierarchical temporal image representation
Authors: Liping Chen; Wende Li; Antonio M. Lopes; Min Zhu; Pengpeng Chen; Mo Yuen Chow
Abstract: With the rapid deployment of Lithium-Ion Batteries (LIBs) in electric vehicles and energy storage systems, inherent operational risks and potential failures have become increasingly evident. Accurate and intelligent diagnosis of incipient battery faults has therefore emerged as a critical challenge. To address the limitations of traditional time-series signal analysis methods in detecting early-stage anomalies, this paper proposes a dual-channel image representation framework that integrates the Markov Transition Field (MTF) and Gramian Angular Summation Field (GASF). These representations are further processed through a Swin-Transformer-based feature extraction module and a HiFuse feature fusion module to develop a novel battery fault diagnosis algorithm. Specifically, raw voltage time-series data are transformed into MTF and GASF images to capture both temporal dynamics and global signal patterns. A dual-channel Swin-Transformer architecture is then employed to simultaneously extract deep representations from the two image modalities. Finally, the HiFuse module enables efficient cross-channel feature fusion, enhancing the model ability to capture discriminative fault-related information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves diagnostic accuracy, recall, and F1-score compared with various traditional approaches for early battery fault identification. These findings validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed algorithm for intelligent early-stage battery fault diagnosis, providing a feasible and efficient solution for battery condition monitoring and safety management.

Title: Multi-Scale Agarwal-Gotman Masking for Transient-Preserving Variational Mode Decomposition in Bearing Fault Diagnosis
Authors: G. L. Priya; K. Krishnendu
Abstract: Efficient extraction of fault-related transients from machinery vibration signals is important for early condition monitoring. Traditional signal decomposition methods, such as empirical mode decomposition (EMD), suffer from mode mixing, whereas variational mode decomposition (VMD) enforces spectral compactness uniformly over time and does not explicitly prioritize the short-duration impulsive segments that represent bearing defects. This paper proposes a multi-scale Agarwal-Gotman energy operator mask (MS-AGOM) integrated into VMD cost functional to achieve transient-preserving decomposition. Multiple dilated AGO operators are computed over a scale set and combined into a single confidence mask by an adaptive reliability weighting mechanism. The formulation is solved by the augmented Lagrangian method employing the alternating-direction method of multipliers (ADMM) technique with guaranteed convergence. A method is also proposed to compute the optimum value of the hyperparameters required in the VMD computation. Experiments on rolling element bearing vibration signal shows that the proposed transient-focused decomposition is a robust and interpretable tool to condition monitoring in industry.

Title: A novel wind turbine bearing fault diagnosis method based on High-Order Spectrum Analysis (HOSA) and YOLOv12
Authors: Taskeen Zahra; Wenyi Liu
Abstract: Due to the growing popularity of wind energy, its construction reliability is becoming a high priority engineering issue regarding the maintenance of wind turbine parts, mainly, bearings. This paper proposes a combined fault-diagnosis pipeline that can integrate High-Order Spectral Analysis (HOSA) object detection framework YOLOv12. The bearing data set based on vibration data was transformed into a set of bispectrum images through HOSA, which enhanced the phase coupled non-linear components. We used these bispectrum images to train YOLOv12 on a multi-class task of bearing conditions including Normal, Inner Race Fault, Outer Race Fault and Ball Fault. The experimental setup is very simple, a model is trained on 2000 bispectrum images (500 images per class), and standard measurements of detection performance are applied. The proposed system produced a 99.90% precision and a 100% recall with a 99.5% of mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5). Such outcomes demonstrate the almost perfect classification accuracy. The independency and generalization ability of the model on all the fault types was shown further through F1-confidence analysis, precision–recall curves, and confusion matrices. The HOSA-YOLOv12 integration is used to achieve an effective, fast, and scalable solution of detecting faults in bearings of wind turbines accurately. This research proves that deep-learning powered spectral diagnostic is feasible and establishes a model of intelligent and condition-based maintenance of renewable energy systems.

Title: Research on Simplifying the Artificial Intelligence Algorithms Development for Status Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis of Typical Nuclear Equipment
Authors: Haidong Wang; Junwei Hou; Zhaosheng Zhang; Xiaochen Shi
Abstract: In order to realize the online status monitoring and fault diagnosis of typical equipment during the operation of nuclear power plants, and to improve the timeliness of status monitoring and fault diagnosis of nuclear power plants, a technical framework of status monitoring and fault diagnosis based on artificial intelligence algorithms is proposed from the practical application level. Use common machine learning and deep learning technologies in the field of artificial intelligence to train different model algorithms through historical data of nuclear power plant operation, including normal data and abnormal data under different failure events. By comparing the test accuracy of different models, the most accurate condition monitoring model and fault diagnosis model are selected to apply to the online state prediction of nuclear power plants. When using real-time data to make online judgments on the state of nuclear power plants, first call the state monitoring model to monitor the abnormal working conditions of the nuclear power plant. Once the abnormal occurrence of the nuclear power plant is monitored, the fault diagnosis model is called to judge the abnormal event, and the fault of the nuclear power plant can be maintained and eliminated in time. Through the analysis and verification of the real data from a typical pump in a certain nuclear power plant in China, it is proved that the proposed calculation framework can be applied to the status monitoring and fault diagnosis of nuclear power plants. For nuclear O&M engineers who lack experience in developing artificial intelligence algorithms, this approach can reduce the difficulty of their development.

Title: Towards Open-Set Fault Diagnosis for Belt Conveyors Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
Authors: Huayang Lv; Fei Liu; Ruiqing Tang; Isaack Kamanga; Guo Zhu; Yunshen Chen; Aokang Zhang; Xu Yang; Xian Zhou
Abstract: Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR)-based distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) has been proven effective for large-scale industrial condition monitoring, especially for belt conveyor monitoring, which requires long-distance distributed vibration sensing. However, current DAS-based conveyor diagnosis is limited by the fixed closed-set assumption, under which all fault categories are presumed to be known during training. This assumption becomes restrictive in long-term monitoring because reliable fault labels are scarce and new fault patterns may emerge as conveyor components degrade. As a result, unseen faults can be forced into known categories with overconfident diagnostic results, increasing the risk of misdiagnosis and reducing diagnostic reliability. To address this problem, we propose Open-Set Masked Autoencoder-Vision Transformer with Support Verification (OS-MVS), an open-set fault diagnosis framework with post-rejection incremental adaptation for DAS-monitored belt conveyors. Instead of treating label scarcity, unknown-fault rejection, and model updating as separate tasks, OS-MVS follows a unified support-space learning principle: it constructs compact known-class support regions from unlabeled and few labeled DAS Mel-spectrograms, verifies whether a test sample belongs to these regions for open-set rejection, and expands the known support space after rejected samples are confirmed as new fault categories. Field experiments on a 5-km coal-mine belt conveyor show that OS-MVS achieves 0.9420 open-set accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.9833 with 5% labeled data, while maintaining stable performance after incremental updates. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of OS-MVS for DAS-based conveyor fault diagnosis under label-scarce, open-set, and long-term monitoring conditions.

Title: Toward Intelligent Fault Diagnosis in Renewable Energy Systems: Integrating Data-Driven and Model-Based Approaches Under Variable Environmental Conditions
Authors: Marouane Marzouk; Majdi Mansouri; Ahmed Anis Kahloul; Marwen Kermani; Anis Sakly; Hazem Nounou
Abstract: Renewable energy systems, including solar photovoltaic arrays and wind turbines, operate under highly variable environmental and operating conditions. Factors such as changing irradiance, temperature fluctuations, wind variability, and component aging make Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) particularly challenging. Therefore, developing reliable, accurate, and interpretable diagnostic methods is essential to ensure system efficiency, safety, and long-term operation. Traditional model-based approaches, which rely on physical system models, offer clear interpretability and solid theoretical foundations. However, their effectiveness can be limited by modeling inaccuracies and difficulties in capturing complex nonlinear behaviors. On the other hand, data-driven and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques have demonstrated strong capabilities in pattern recognition and fault classification, but often face challenges related to data dependence, limited transparency, and reduced robustness under unseen conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive and structured review of FDD techniques for renewable energy systems, covering model-based, signal-based, data-driven, and hybrid approaches. A unified perspective is presented to clarify the strengths, limitations, and application domains of each category. Particular attention is given to recent advances in hybrid methods that combine physical modeling and AI, including feature fusion, ensemble learning, attention-based models, and transfer learning. Moreover, advanced signal processing techniques are discussed for their role in extracting meaningful features from noisy and non-stationary data. Rather than ranking methods by headline accuracy, which has become saturated and is only weakly comparable across heterogeneous datasets, the review adopts a critical, deployment-oriented perspective that emphasizes cross-condition robustness, standardized benchmarking, and the constraints of real-world deployment. The review also highlights the growing importance of digital twin technology as a promising framework for next-generation FDD systems, enabling real-time monitoring, adaptive learning, and predictive maintenance. Furthermore, Explainable AI is explored as a key direction for improving the transparency and trustworthiness of AI-based diagnostic models. Finally, the paper identifies major challenges and open research issues, such as data scarcity, generalization among different operating conditions, computational efficiency, and system reliability. Future research directions are outlined toward developing more robust, adaptive, and interpretable FDD solutions that can operate effectively in dynamic and uncertain environments.

Title: Small Sample Fault Diagnosis Using Gap-Regularized Loss and Multiscale Attention CNN
Authors: Lihao Ye; Ke Zhang; Bin Jiang; Silvio Simani; Xue Li
Abstract: In aerospace engine systems, reliable fault diagnosis is essential for ensuring operational safety, yet the scarcity of labeled fault data remains a major obstacle. Although massive amounts of operational signals are routinely collected, expert annotation is costly and limited, leading to small-sample learning challenges, where only a limited number of labeled samples are available for model training. To address this issue, we propose a diagnostic framework tailored for such label-scarce scenarios. Specifically, a multiscale attentive convolutional neural network is constructed to enhance discriminative representation by integrating multiscale feature extraction with squeeze-and-excitation attention. More importantly, a Gap-regularized loss function is introduced to jointly enforce intraclass compactness and interclass separability, thereby improving generalization when only limited labeled data are available. Extensive experiments on two aerospace engine-related datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic accuracy in limited-labeled-data settings, highlighting its potential for intelligent health monitoring in safety-critical aerospace applications.
