However, collecting fault data by inducing faults in high-capacity or highspeed machines is often unsafe and impractical, which limits the application of traditional supervised learning approaches. Zero-shot diagnosis addresses this by enabling fault detection without fault data from the target machine, but current approaches struggle with scalability and generalization across different machine types, capacities, and operating conditions due to restrictive domain transfer assumptions that limit adaptability. Two different scalable fault modeling approaches are introduced to enable accurate diagnosis in target high-capacity or high-speed systems without requiring any fault data from those systems, thereby achieving zero-sample fault diagnosis under practical operational constraints. The first method uses constrained maximum likelihood linear regression (CMLLR) on latent features to synthesize representative fault data for the target machine from healthy-condition data. The second method maps source and target features into a domain-invariant feature space (DIFS), allowing a single model to generalize across machines with varying capacity. Fault modeling in the DIFS is further extended to address scalable speed modeling, using source data from the machine operating at low RPM to detect faults at high RPM, without requiring any fault condition data at higher RPM. Experimental validation on generator, gearbox systems and a publicly available benchmark dataset demonstrates that the proposed methods achieve robust and generalizable fault diagnosis under zero-sample conditions.

This work provides a scalable and deployable diagnostic solution for one of the most demanding industrial environments in existence.

Title: Attention-Guided Coati-Optimized GAF-DenseNet169 for Fault Diagnosis in Electric Vehicle Drive Systems
Authors: Emrah Aslan
Abstract: Reliable fault diagnosis of electric vehicle (EV) drive systems is essential for ensuring operational safety, predictive maintenance, and propulsion system reliability. Induction motors used in EV applications may be exposed to several electrical and loading abnormalities, including overload fault (OLF), overvoltage fault (OVF), undervoltage fault (UVF), phase-to-ground fault (PTGF), and phase-to-phase fault (PTPF). In this study, an attention-guided fault-diagnosis framework named COA-CBAM-GAF-DenseNet169 is proposed by integrating Gramian angular field (GAF) signal imaging, DenseNet169-based transfer learning, convolutional block attention module (CBAM), and the coati optimization algorithm (COA). First, raw motor signals are separated using a leakage-free sequence-level protocol and converted into Gramian angular summation field (GASF) images to preserve temporal dependencies in a two-dimensional representation. Then, a pretrained DenseNet169 backbone extracts deep feature maps from the generated GAF images. To enhance fault-related feature discrimination, a CBAM attention block is inserted after the DenseNet169 feature extractor, enabling both channel-wise and spatial attention refinement. COA is used to optimize the learning rate, dropout rate, dense layer size, batch size, fine-tuning depth, CBAM reduction ratio, CBAM spatial kernel size, and feature-weighting coefficients. Experimental results show that the proposed COA-CBAM-GAF-DenseNet169 model achieves 98.30% accuracy, 98.42% precision, 98.30% recall, 98.28% F1-score, and 99.21% macro-AUC, outperforming standalone transfer learning models, XGBoost-based hybridization, attention-free DenseNet169, and alternative optimization strategies. Ablation analysis, repeated-run statistical validation, robustness testing, computational burden evaluation, and Grad-CAM visualization further confirm the contribution and reliability of the proposed framework. The results indicate that the proposed attention-guided and coati-optimized model provides an accurate, interpretable, and near-real-time capable diagnostic framework for EV induction motor drive systems.

Title: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on AVMD and HPO-DBN
Authors: Xinyu Sha; Fucai Qian
Abstract: To overcome difficulties such as non-stationary vibrations, high-dimensional feature redundancy, and mode selection issues that may arise during signal decomposition in bearing fault diagnosis. Next, the Relief F algorithm is employed to select desired features, and an autoencoder is used to reduce the selected features dimensionally. Furthermore, because the Hunter-Prey Optimisation (HPO) algorithm can balance multiple objectives during the search process by utilising the concepts of hunter and prey to generate a better solution set, incorporating this algorithm into the Deep Belief Network (DBN) establishes an HPO-DBN fault diagnosis model. Subsequently, we validate the proposed method using both public datasets and field compressor data. Moreover, we compare the results with those obtained from the Support Vector Machine (SVM). The findings indicate that this approach enhances the bearing fault identification rate, thus supporting predictive maintenance of bearings.

Title: Physics-guided adaptive spectral transformation for unsupervised cross-domain vibration-based compound fault diagnosis
Authors: Eatedal Alabdulkreem; Zohaib Mushtaq; Abdulrahman Ahmed Gharawi; Ammar Almutawa; Sakher Ghanem; Ali Daud
Abstract: Diagnosing multiple faults that are simultaneously occurring in a rotating machinery is theoretically a domain adaptation problem where different defect sizes cause systematic spectral changes which make the standard classifiers assumption of identically distributed data invalid. Current unsupervised domain adaptation methods make use of marginal alignment through multi-kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MK-MMD) or adversarial training. They are not explicitly imposing a physical constraint on the variability of defect scale which suggests that they are likely to fail in negative transfer and harmonic decoupling. This work introduces a physics-informed adaptive spectral transformation (PGAST) method that consists of three main elements. A severity-aware spectral transformation unit that first separates the signal into frequency bands and then a signal-dependent warping coefficient is applied with the help of time-domain and spectral regularization. A Lipschitz-stabilized 1D-CNN encoder that obtains domain-invariant features at a controlled sensitivity and a spectral-aware class-conditional MMD objective that aligns feature distributions separately across low, mid, and high-frequency regimes which help avoid inter-class mode mixing. When tested on the publicly available bearing datasets with different defect diameters, PGAST leads to 95.96% cross-domain recognition accuracy showing the capability to generalize to unseen compound couplings. This suggests that the use of structured physics-informed alignment is an improvement over the purely statistical baselines.

Title: Multi-Band Noise-Adaptive DEMON with SNR-Weighted Fusion for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
Authors: Jagadish S. Jakati; S. S. Ittannavar; Raju Hebbale; S. Mahadevaswamy; B. P. Pradeep Kumar; Bhavaling Alias Pratima Khot
Abstract: Multi-Band Noise-Adaptive DEMON with SNR-Weighted Fusion for Bearing Fault Diagnosis addresses the inherent sensitivity of classical DEMON to manual band selection and band-dependent noise. The objective of this work is to design a machine-agnostic demodulation framework that preserves fault-induced impulsiveness while remaining robust across heterogeneous spectral conditions. To this end, the vibration signal is decomposed into multiple spectrally diverse sub-bands, each processed through envelope demodulation. A noise-aware fusion mechanism is then introduced, where band-wise contributions are adaptively weighted using a detection signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) criterion, emphasizing diagnostically dominant channels and suppressing noise-dominated responses. Experiments conducted on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset employ group-wise statistics, window-wise trend analysis, qualitative waveform inspection, and ablation studies. The results demonstrate that the proposed method preserves the physical characteristics of bearing faults, yielding significantly higher impulsiveness in defective samples (kurtosis ≈ 5-7) compared to healthy conditions (≈ 2.6-2.8), while producing smoother and more stable diagnostic trajectories across time windows. Compared with single-band DEMON and equal-weight multi-band fusion, the adaptive strategy consistently improves robustness without degrading performance on clean benchmark data. These findings confirm that noise-adaptive fusion eliminates the brittleness of manual band selection and establishes a principled, interpretable foundation for scalable fault monitoring in both benchmark and industrial environments.

Title: A hybrid cross-domain few-shot bearing fault diagnosis method combining multi-scale feature association and physical information
Authors: Changfu He; Nanyan Gai; Ke Yan; Haidong Shao
Abstract: Cross-domain fault diagnosis of bearings constitutes a cornerstone of mechanical-system condition monitoring and intelligent maintenance. Although existing cross-domain fault diagnosis methods have made progress in alleviating the performance degradation caused by domain shift, most studies neglect physical information in fault diagnosis under complex cross-machine few-shot conditions. To this end, a cross-domain few-shot bearing fault diagnosis method through multi-scale feature association and physical information (PICDF) is proposed. Firstly, a Laplace wavelet kernel function that integrates the sampling frequency and fault feature frequency (FWK) is introduced, aiming to incorporate physical information into the feature extraction network’s structure. This integration guides the PICDF to learn the mechanism characteristics of bearing faults. Secondly, the feature extraction network with a new multi-scale feature association fusion block is designed to capture the multi-level correlations between cross-domain features, enabling the effective fusion of features across different scales. Lastly, an unsupervised cross-domain multi-adaptation strategy is proposed, which integrates the few-shot learning method to enhance the discriminability and domain transferability of features, reduce distribution discrepancies between cross-domain features, and decrease reliance on labeled fault samples. Experimental results in multiple cross-condition and cross-machine few-shot fault diagnosis tasks demonstrate that PICDF has more significant advantages in diagnostic accuracy, robustness, and domain adaptability than seven recent cross-domain fault diagnosis methods. Additionally, ablation experiments further verified the contribution and necessity of the proposed strategy to the diagnostic performance.

Title: Intelligent fault diagnosis of roller bearings using a transfer learning-based dual-input spectrogram–scalogram convolutional neural network model
Authors: Rahul Singh; Ragita Ojha; Suraj P. Harsha
Abstract: This research proposes DiSCNet (Dual-input Spectrogram–Scalogram Convolutional Network), a dual-input convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for robust and highly accurate bearing fault diagnosis using time–frequency representations of vibration signals. The model is trained end-to-end on matched spectrogram–scalogram image pairs generated from vibration signals acquired experimentally from a bearing test rig. The results highlight the advantages of integrating spectral and wavelet-domain features into a unified deep learning framework. By effectively leveraging complementary information from both domains, DiSCNet enhances feature discriminability and class separability, making it a highly promising approach for practical industrial condition-monitoring and fault-diagnosis applications.

Title: Adapting Without Source Data: High-Confidence Knowledge-Guided Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Rotating Machinery Fault Diagnosis
Authors: Xue Ding; Aidong Deng; Yang Liu; Wenbin Bian; Meng Xu
Abstract: The accurate condition monitoring of rotating machinery relies on the stability of the vibration measurement-to-decision mapping. In practical deployments, variations in operating conditions, together with source-free constraints, where the historical source data are unavailable, often induce distribution shifts in vibration measurements, leading to unstable representations and unreliable fault diagnosis. To address this challenge, a high-confidence knowledge-guided source-free domain adaptation network (HCKNet) is proposed. Within this framework, a confident anchor-induced self-refinement (CASR) mechanism is designed to purify noisy pseudo-labels by exploiting high-confidence target anchors as structural priors, which mitigates error accumulation and stabilizes the adaptation process. In addition, a cross-space consistency regularization (CSCR) mechanism is formulated as a complementary constraint to suppress the residual local prediction inconsistency and improve decision consistency under the domain shift. Experimental results on two datasets demonstrate that HCKNet achieves a consistently more reliable and robust vibration measurement-to-decision mapping under source-free deployment.

Title: Cyclic Spectral Coherence Map-Based Filter Design With Geometric Mean Optimization for Industrial Fault Diagnosis
Authors: Sumika Chauhan; Govind Vashishtha; Hamid Shiri; Justyna Hebda Sobkowicz; Radoslaw Zimroz

The designed filter is a valuable tool for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance, contributing to operational efficiency, preventing costly breakdowns, and maintaining a safe working environment.

Title: Integrated Bearing Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis via Distribution-Adaptive Composite Correlation Under Mixed Gaussian-Laplace Noise
Authors: Wei Fan; Shaofeng Hou; Liling Han; Chao Chen; Zhongkui Zhu; Long Chen
Abstract: Bearing condition monitoring is essential in ensuring the reliable operation of machinery. Yet most vibration-analysis techniques implicitly assume Gaussian noise - a premise often violated in practice, where signals contain Laplace components or Gaussian-Laplace mixtures. To overcome this limitation, we propose a distribution-adaptive composite correlation (DACC) framework that simultaneously performs condition monitoring and early fault diagnosis under mixed Gaussian-Laplace noise. First, the classical noise-resistant correlation (NRC) is generalized to remain robust against heavy-tailed Laplace disturbances and broadband Gaussian interference. This generalized NRC is fused with the frequency-domain energy ratio to form a composite correlation that accentuates fault-related impulses while suppressing stochastic fluctuations. Integrating the composite correlation over a sliding window yields a scalar health index that evolves monotonically with bearing degradation. Title: Signal Enhancement Method for Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery Under Strong Attenuation Conditions Based on Analog–Digital Collaboration

Abstract: Traditional envelope demodulation methods (e.g., Fast Kurtogram, Auto-gram) encounter two key challenges in rotating machinery fault diagnosis: (1.) Under strong attenuation, signal amplitudes below the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) quantization resolution cause information loss, rendering digital-domain methods (including deep learning) ineffective. A tunable resonant circuit amplifies the target frequency band (e.g., bearing fault characteristic frequencies) at the ADC front-end, increasing the signal attenuation cutoff frequency from 10 kHz to > 50 kHz. This over-comes quantization resolution limitations and restores high-frequency fault signals. Bearing test bench experiments show that enhanced data exhibits vibration waveform pulse intensity and phase characteristics highly consistent with reference data. The Fast Kurtogram envelope spectrum clearly reveals 1 × and high-order fault frequency components, with significantly improved fault feature recognition compared to unenhanced data. This “hardware enhancement + algorithm optimization” cross-domain collaborative approach improves diagnostic reliability for rotating machinery un-der strong attenuation conditions, offering a robust solution for complex scenario condition monitoring.

Title: Swin Transformer for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
Authors: Jae Woo Yoon; Su Jin Seol; Byeong Woo Kim
Abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis requires models that remain robust under diverse and noisy industrial environments. Experimental results indicated that the proposed model achieved the highest classification accuracy and superior robustness and computational efficiency in both noise-free and strong-noise environments.

The proposed method is validated through simulation studies on a gas generator rotor system, and an aero-engine simulation models under diverse speed conditions. Finally, the experimental validation of unbalance fault diagnosis on a real aero-engine rotor demonstrates that even under complex transmission paths, the proposed method achieves high-accuracy diagnostic performance.

Title: Time–frequency fully-connected graph neural network: An effective multiscale spatiotemporal dependency learning method for multisource machine fault diagnosis
Authors: Yadong Xu; Sheng Li; Zhihan Li; Kaili Wu; Ruyi Huang; Beibei Sun; J. C. Ji
Abstract: The rapid evolution of sensing technologies and multi-source data fusion has created unprecedented opportunities for advanced condition monitoring and fault diagnosis in intelligent manufacturing. In this context, numerous multi-source signal-based diagnostic methods have been proposed. However, most existing methods still struggle to extract intricate coupling relationships and lack the capacity for holistic spatiotemporal modeling of high-dimensional data. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel framework termed the Time–Frequency Fully Connected Graph Neural Network (TF-FC-GNN) for multi-source machinery fault diagnosis. Specifically, a dual-stream time–frequency learning architecture is designed in conjunction with a multi-graph construction strategy to facilitate the extraction of rich features and explicitly model inter-sensor couplings across both domains. A spatiotemporal fully connected graph neural network is embedded within each stream to comprehensively capture dependencies across heterogeneous sensors and multiple temporal scales. Subsequently, a multi-domain feature fusion module (MFFM) is introduced to perform both intra-domain and cross-domain feature alignment, thereby enhancing representational consistency. Finally, an improved online label smoothing (IOLS) algorithm is incorporated, which dynamically utilizes intermediate prediction labels to generate more personalized and robust supervisory information. Extensive experiments conducted on both a public gearbox benchmark and a self-collected industrial gearbox dataset demonstrate that TF-FC-GNN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in diagnostic accuracy. These results validate the superior effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed approach.

Title: Dual-mode dynamic modeling of a brushless direct current motor transmission system for intelligent fault diagnosis
Authors: Dingfan Yang; Hong Zou; Xingwu Zhang; Shuhui Wang; Jiawei Xiang
Abstract: Brushless direct current (BLDC) motor transmission systems are widely used in smart household and other consumer electromechanical products, where compact integration and dual-mode power transmission are often required. To realize different transmission functions within limited installation space, such transmission systems usually operate in two distinct modes, namely a planetary-transmission mode and a rigid-driveline mode. Since these two modes exhibit significantly different dynamic characteristics, a single-mode model is insufficient for accurate vibration description and fault-oriented data generation. To address this issue, this paper develops dual-mode dynamic models of a BLDC motor transmission system for intelligent fault diagnosis under limited measured fault data. First, two mode-dependent dynamic models are established and iteratively updated using measured healthy signals to improve the consistency between simulation and experiment. Next, localized gear defects are introduced into the planetary-transmission model, whereas bearing inner-race and outer-race defects are incorporated into the rigid-driveline model, thereby generating abundant labeled fault signals. Finally, the synthesized datasets are used to train representative artificial-intelligence models, which are then evaluated using measured fault signals under sample-limited settings. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves up to 100.00% accuracy and 100.00% F1-score under the merged 9-class setting, providing a practical route for health monitoring of consumer motor transmission systems with limited measured fault data.

Title: Physics-guided deep learning-based domain-shift robust alignment network for bearing fault diagnosis
Authors: Abdulrahman Ahmed Gharawi; Zohaib Mushtaq; Saud Yonbawi; Ammar Almutawa; Sakher Ghanem; Ali Daud

Traditional domain adaptation methods often rely on large over-parameterised backbones or adversarial training, suffering from negative transfer and poor interpretability. Rigorous ablation and statistical analysis confirm the indispensable roles of each component.

Title: Beyond CNN or Transformer Alone: A GADF-Powered Dual-Branch Network With KAN-Swin Transformer for Fault Diagnosis of Aerospace Bearing
Authors: Liubing Hu; Jinghong Tian; Zhilin Dong; Lingli Cui; Chengri Lang
Abstract: To address the critical challenges of submerged weak fault signatures and extreme operational variability in aerospace bearing diagnosis, a GADF-powered dual-branch network with KAN-Swin Transformer is proposed for fault diagnosis of aerospace bearing in this study. Subsequently, a KAN-Swin Transformer module is developed by replacing traditional multilayer perceptron with B-spline basis functions, which enhances nonlinear mapping capability through dynamic grid adjustment strategy, effectively reducing parameter complexity while improving modeling of transient impacts and periodic patterns. Furthermore, a dual-branch parallel architecture is proposed: The KAN-Swin Transformer branch extracts local structural features through hierarchical window attention mechanisms, while the CNN-GAM branch strengthens global texture perception via multi-scale convolution integrated with channel-spatial attention fusion. Finally, cross-modal feature concatenation is combined with adaptive pooling to achieve synergistic optimization of global-local characteristics, significantly enhancing fault pattern discriminability under complex noise environments. The developed method tested on two different sets of aerospace bearing data, has achieved a classification accuracy of 100%. Meanwhile, the collaborative effect of module integration including KAN, Swin Transformer and CNN-GAM is validated through ablation experiments, showing enhanced cross-speed operational recognition rates compared to baseline models and confirming the robustness of the framework against noise and variable loading conditions. By synergistically integrating mechanism fusion and attention architectures, the proposed framework provides a reliable solution for intelligent health monitoring of aerospace bearings. Future work may focus on computational optimization and multi-sensor fusion for real-time aerospace diagnostics.

Title: Gearbox Anomaly Detection in Wind Turbines Using Classical Machine Learning
Authors: Duy Tran; Pedro Lind; Arvind Keprate
Abstract: The primary goal of this paper is to develop a data-driven model that can classify or predict the anomalies of wind turbines’ gearboxes by applying machine learning techniques. Owing to the tremendous demand for wind energy, the turbines move offshore and continue growing in size and number. Consequently, this will result in an increment of operational and maintenance costs, which simultaneously poses many challenges for the wind industry. From the literature review, studies highlighted the drivetrain and gearbox as being responsible for major failures and the downtime of wind turbines. This paper examines the most typical malfunctioning modes of the wind turbine gearbox. The importance and evolution of operational condition monitoring are covered. Subsequently, a data-driven approach is considered, and the possibilities of various experimentations are discussed. A machine learning pipeline with classification algorithms is developed to distinguish between healthy and damaged scenarios. The accuracy of the methods applied in this paper is verified with the actual healthy and damaged vibratory signals from a reference wind turbine gearbox. This can open the gate to further investigations and real-time applications for condition monitoring of wind turbines’ gearboxes under harsh operational environments.

Title: Early Fault Detection in Pump Systems Using Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Techniques
Authors: Hoang Anh Dang; Dung Dao-Van; Dat Nguyen-Tien; Nhat Hai Nguyen
Abstract: In industrial settings, unexpected equipment failures can have severe consequences, impacting both economic performance and human safety. Detecting or predicting potential failures at an early stage is crucial, as it lays the foundation for predictive maintenance strategies that optimize machine utilization and prevent costly downtimes. However, a major challenge in industrial applications is the lack of labeled data, which limits the effectiveness of supervised learning approach. Therefore, researchers have recently focused on unsupervised learning approaches to address anomaly detection. This paper investigates a case study of a pump operational dataset. Four anomaly detection algorithms (HBOS, KNN, LOF, and Isolation Forest) are selected and compared for their effectiveness in early failure detection. The results show that HBOS and Isolation Forest detect anomalies more effectively. Beside, HBOS is somewhat less effective in identifying early signs of impending failures. The goal is to apply machine learning algorithms to identify abnormal patterns in the data before actual failures occur, thereby enhancing predictive maintenance capabilities. This research contributes to improving industrial reliability by enabling proactive measures against equipment malfunctions.

Title: Anomaly Detection in Wind Turbines Using Variational Autoencoders and Isolation Forest
Authors: Guillermo Gil de Avalle Bellido; Christos Emmanouilidis
Abstract: Wind turbines are susceptible to failure events which reduce operational availability, increase costs and introduce safety hazards. Anomaly detection can be used to identify failure events or provide early warnings of faults. Many industrial installations rely on fault detection methods based on static thresholds over parameters estimated from the condition monitoring data, following established standards. However, static thresholds may fail to capture the variability of operational contexts and the individual turbines’ behaviour. Adaptive machine learning methods offer instead data-driven adaptation flexibility. However, this flexibility is restricted by the narrow range of situations which the operational data are drawn from, mostly corresponding to normal operating states or a limited set of failure events. To address such challenges, this study combines a Variational Autoencoder with an Isolation Forest to effectively capture anomalies. The performance of this method is evaluated against static thresholds recommended in established standards over benchmarking data from the domain, as well as additional operational data from wind turbines. Results indicate that, while static thresholds may suffice in simpler scenarios, they often fail in more complex operational ones. In contrast, the proposed model demonstrates adaptation capacity and is more successful in detecting anomalies even with noisy and sparse data, indicating promising operational potential for industry.

Title: Fhepdm: Fully Homomorphic Encryption Secured Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Wind Turbines Predictive Maintenance
Authors: Jinxiang Dai; Shancang Li
Abstract: In wind power generation, equipment anomalies and cyber threats impose substantial operational and economic risks. While multi-party data sharing among turbine manufacturers, operators, and analytics providers could improve anomaly detection, privacy issues restrict collaboration. This paper proposes FHEPdM (Fully Homomorphic Encryption-enabled Secure Collaborative Anomaly Detection Architecture), a novel framework enabling privacy-preserving multi-party predictive maintenance without revealing sensitive data. Utilizing fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), it trains and infers a lightweight logistic regression model on encrypted Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) data for end-to-end confidentiality. Integrated with a hybrid Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman-fully homomorphic encryption (ECDH-FHE) key management system, it reduces latency while upholding 128-bit security. Evaluation on the Wind Turbine SCADA Dataset yields 0.979 accuracy, 0.52 membership inference attack success, and 17-minute training, delivering a practical, scalable solution for secure industrial cooperation in wind systems.

Title: Multi-order nonstationarity-driven cointegration method for wind turbine generator condition monitoring and anomaly detection
Authors: Nasir H.R. Syed; Debela A. Teklemariyem; Abu Al Hassan; Phong B. Dao
Abstract: Wind turbine Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) data are inherently nonstationary due to changing environmental conditions, operating regimes, and component aging, while emerging faults can further alter the statistical stationarity behavior of monitoring parameters. These characteristics make reliable condition monitoring and fault detection particularly challenging. This paper proposes a novel multi-order nonstationarity-driven cointegration framework for wind turbine monitoring that explicitly accounts for variables with different levels of nonstationarity. Using Johansen’s cointegration method, long-term equilibrium relationships are identified from the training data, and normalized cointegrating vectors are estimated. Cointegration residuals are then obtained by projecting SCADA data onto these vectors. Stationary residuals from the training set are used to establish control limits, while monitoring statistics, based on the Mahalanobis distance, are calculated using stationary residuals from the testing set. An alarm is triggered when these statistics exceed the defined threshold. The proposed approach is validated through a numerical study involving simulated faults in time series with different nonstationarity levels, followed by application to real SCADA data from a commercial wind turbine. Results demonstrate that the method effectively handles multi-order nonstationarity and enables accurate early detection of generator faults. The proposed framework detected the faults approximately 40 min and 33 h and 7 min earlier than the actual occurrence of generator bearing damage on August 20, 2017, at 06:08 and generator damage on August 21, 2017, at 14:47. The early detection capability highlights its potential to improve the robustness and reliability of wind turbine condition monitoring systems compared to principal component analysis and partial least squares.

Title: Dynamic Health Index Construction and Early Anomaly Detection for Wind Turbines via LSTM Autoencoders
Authors: Xiaomin Zhao; Lin Pan; Shunfeng Dai; Keyun Peng
Abstract: Wind energy conversion systems operate under complex, fluctuating, and largely uncontrollable environmental conditions, making early anomaly detection a key requirement for ensuring turbine reliability and reducing operation and maintenance costs. Existing SCADA-based monitoring approaches typically rely on manually engineered features, static thresholds, or labeled fault data, and thus struggle to capture the nonlinear temporal dynamics of three-phase currents. To address these challenges, this study develops an end-to-end, unsupervised health modeling framework based on a Long Short-Term Memory Autoencoder (LSTM-AE). By learning the temporal patterns of healthy three-phase currents and constructing a dynamic health index, the framework enables sensitive detection of deviations from nominal behavior. Experimental results show that the proposed model exhibits stable convergence during training, learns highly discriminative bottleneck representations, and achieves high sensitivity to early anomalies on real wind farm data. Comparative analyses further demonstrate that the dynamic health index offers greater robustness than conventional static-threshold methods in adapting to changing operating conditions and suppressing false alarms. Overall, the proposed framework provides a transferable technical paradigm for unsupervised early anomaly detection of wind turbines under real-world operating conditions.

Title: M-wave Event Stream Transformer for Mechanical Anomaly Detection of GIS Circuit Breakers
Authors: Yanmeng Wu; Siyuan Liu; Huidong Tian; Jinxia Long
Abstract: Mechanical faults in circuit breakers of gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) are a major threat to the safe operation of power grids. But existing diagnostic methods depend a lot on manual feature extraction, do not catch time dependencies among event points, and have big model sizes not good for edge deployment. This paper gives a new event-stream Transformer Autoencoder for unsupervised mechanical anomaly detection of GIS circuit breakers. Raw coil current waveforms (M-waves) are turned into structured event sequences with key points (T0, T1, T3, T5) and time differences, current values, and auxiliary switch asynchrony. Statistics show a big difference between opening and closing operations, so we use a separate modelling strategy. A small Transformer Autoencoder (0.28M parameters) uses self-attention to catch time dependencies among events. Mixed modelling of opening and closing samples gives false positives because of distribution mismatch, but separate modelling finds anomalies with low reconstruction error on normal samples. Experimental results demonstrate that separate modeling reduces the false positive rate from 23.7% to 1.7% for closing and 3.7% for opening operations, and achieves an inference time of 2.3 ms per sample on an edge device. This work provides a practical, low-latency solution for real-time condition monitoring of GIS circuit breakers in smart grids, contributing to the reliability and intelligence of advanced energy systems and power electronics.

Title: Explainable Physics-Informed Hybrid Modeling for Anomaly Detection and Structural Fatigue Assessment in Wind Turbines Using SCADA Data

Abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly essential for trustworthy decision-making in wind energy systems, particularly for anomaly detection and condition monitoring using SCADA data. While recent studies have achieved high accuracy in short-term power forecasting, they often rely on black-box models and fail to account for long-term structural fatigue. The proposed approach integrates a random forest–XGBoost stacking ensemble with a Palmgren–Miner-based fatigue index to capture cumulative structural degradation under variable wind conditions. Hyperparameter optimization is performed using Optuna to enhance model performance. To improve model transparency, both global and local explainability techniques are incorporated, including the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for global feature importance analysis and LIME for instance-level interpretation. The proposed framework achieved very high predictive performance, with an F1-score of 0.9992, recall of 0.9996, precision of 0.9989, and ROC–AUC of 1.0000. Precision–recall analysis further confirmed strong performance under a class imbalance condition. These results should, however, be interpreted with caution, as the anomaly labels are derived from threshold-based criteria applied to SCADA variables. An ablation study reveals a trade-off between predictive accuracy and physical consistency, showing that the integration of fatigue-related features enhances interpretability and alignment with mechanical degradation processes. Title: SWIFT: Spectral Wavelet Integrated Fault Transformer for Wind Turbine Anomaly Detection
Authors: David S. Yin; Jing Gao

Ablation studies confirm that combining frequency-domain decomposition with multi-scale attention is essential for robust fault detection in offshore wind turbines. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating domain-specific, multi-resolution modeling strategies when analyzing high-dimensional, noisy time series in renewable energy systems.

Title: Time-Localized Wavelet Packet Feature Extraction for Wind Turbine Gearbox Fault Detection
Authors: Nasrin Ramezanzadeh; Subhajit Chatterjee; Hamed Badihi
Abstract: Wind turbine gearboxes operate under variable loading and harsh environmental conditions, making early fault detection essential for reducing turbine downtime and operation and maintenance (O&M) costs. The analysis focuses on the 10 Hz to 40 Hz frequency band, which is physically motivated by the frequency region surrounding the rotational frequency of the high-speed shaft (i.e., 1800 rpm ≈ 30 Hz). Experimental analysis across multiple accelerometer locations shows that the selected subband centered near 34 Hz provides the strongest separation between healthy and damaged gearbox conditions. The proposed time-localized wavelet packet feature extraction framework provides an interpretable and computationally efficient approach for wind turbine gearbox fault detection.

Title: Anomaly Detection in the Task of Remote Monitoring of Large Rotary Machines Based on the Signal-Based Digital Twin
Authors: Jindrich Liska; Jan Jakl; Vojtech Vasicek
Abstract: Anomaly detection plays a crucial role in remote monitoring systems by identifying deviations from normal operating conditions, which may indicate potential faults or performance degradation. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on statistical techniques or rule-based algorithms, which may struggle to capture complex relationships in data and adapt to dynamic operational conditions. In this context, the emerging paradigm of signal-based digital twins offers a promising solution. A signal-based digital twin is a virtual model that mirrors the dynamics of a physical machine based on real-time sensor information. Using advanced data analytics, machine learning algorithms, and physics-based models, signal-based digital twins provide a powerful framework for anomaly detection. Integrating such models into remote monitoring systems for decision-making purposes is one of the current challenges. This approach enables proactive maintenance strategies, reduces unplanned downtime, and increases overall equipment reliability. This paper aims to explore the application of signal-based digital twin for anomaly detection in remote monitoring of large rotating machines. It describes the concept of signal-based digital twin, its representation, clarifies the role in anomaly detection, and presents a case study illustrating the practical use in remote monitoring system. By bridging the gap between data analysis, machine learning, and domain knowledge, signal-based digital twins offer a significant framework for advancing techniques in proactive maintenance, ensuring the reliability, safety, and efficiency of industrial operations.

Title: Black Box++: An Intelligent Iot-Based Flight Data Recorder With Predictive Maintenance and Real-Time Anomaly Detection
Authors: C. S. Kishore Kumar; Madila Kotesh; S. Karthick
Abstract: Flight data recorders, also known as black boxes, play important functions in the analysis of aircraft accident through the recording of the important parameters of the flight. Traditional black box, however, is just a passive recording device, which does not provide any real-time monitoring or predictive services but only offers data retrieval after occurrence of incidents. In this paper the Black Box++ which is a sophisticated embedded flight event recorder system, the one that incorporates real-time sensor monitoring, wireless data uplink, anomaly detection, and predictive maintenance features is presented. Data transmission It uses the LoRa wireless communication and GPS tracking, and an Arduino Uno microcontroller is used to connect to various sensors such as accelerators, temperature sensors, pressure sensors, and GPS modules. An exemplar machine learning model with Random Forests to classify flight phases was found to have remarkably high accuracy of more than 0.98 in all the training set sizes. BMP280 sensor data were successfully used to distinguish between normal and abnormal flight patterns, and the altitude ranged between 7000-14000 meters and the pressure between 70-300 kPa. The analysis of feature importance showed that the key predictor was the altitude (importance: 0.312), then accelerator Z-axis (0.227), temperature (0.178), pressure (0.094) and accelerator Y-axis (0.082). The system also showed stable performance with more than 100 operating hours and a steady sensor health, and predictive maintenance models based on machine learning showed that the remaining useful life could be thus: BMP280 pressure sensor at 122.3 hours, MPU-6050 IMU at 191.3 hours, GPS module at 305.8 hours, and LM35 temperature sensor at 174.0 hours. The flight data anomaly detection was able to detect 12 anomalous events based on Isolation Forest algorithm with an anomaly score of between -6.0 and 4.0. These findings show that Black Box++ has better situational awareness, predictive maintenance scheduling, and better aviation safety due to real-time data analytics and predictive capabilities.

Title: Wavelet-Based Diffusion for Unsupervised Machine Anomaly Detection
Authors: Chang Guo; Jingcheng Wen; Chen Zhang; Zhibin Zhao; Xingwu Zhang
Abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) based on deep learning plays a vital role in predictive maintenance and health monitoring (PHM) of major equipment. However, the black-box nature of the models hinders the deployment in real-world. Wavelet packet transform (WPT) is a well-established and highly interpretable method for analyzing vibration signals in PHM. However, applying it directly to reconstruction-based UAD is challenging. Because of the perfect reconstruction property of the inverse wavelet transform, it almost flawlessly reconstructs both normal and abnormal signals, failing to generate the reconstruction residuals necessary to identify anomalies. To address this, we integrate WPT with diffusion models (DMs), which have demonstrated a promising ability to detect anomalies by learning the manifold of normal data. In this paper, we propose a wavelet diffusion-based method for detecting anomalies in vibration signals. It can be regarded as a data-driven wavelet packet transform, which tries to eliminate failure information in the monitoring signals and consequently detects abnormal health states. Specifically, a learnable wavelet packet transform (LWPT) is firstly utilized to project the raw vibration signals into sub-frequency bands. Then the DM is applied on the first two sub-bands to get the reconstruction sub-bands. The DM enables effective reconstruction of normal signals while exposing deviations indicative of anomalies. At last, the reconstructed signal is built via inverse LWPT using the reconstructed sub-bands and the remaining sub-bands. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on a helicopter main gearbox (MGB) dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves state-of-the-art performance but also provides interpretable insights for users.

Title: Acoustic Emission-Based Anomaly Detection and Statistical Analysis for Predicting Failures in Cast Resin Transformers
Authors: Tae Yun Hong; Du Kyeong Kwon; Young Woo Youn; Jong Ho Sun; Jin Gyu Kim
Abstract: This paper proposes an acoustic emission-based anomaly detection and statistical analysis method to detect partial discharges caused by insulation degradation inside cast resin transformers. While high-frequency current transformers and ultra-high frequency sensors offer high accuracy, they are expensive and require complex signal interpretation. In contrast, acoustic emission sensors can measure elastic waves generated within the insulation at a relatively low cost. By applying artificial intelligence techniques, data-driven anomaly detection can be achieved without complicated analysis procedures. In this study, an acoustic emission sensor was attached to the outer enclosure of a 22.9 kV cast resin transformer to acquire signals under both normal and faulty conditions. The Hilbert transform was applied to enhance impulsive characteristics, and a one-dimensional convolutional long short-term memory autoencoder model was developed for anomaly detection. Using a threshold based on the interquartile range, normal and fault signals were classified with 100% accuracy in the laboratory environment. The proposed method provides an efficient data-driven analytical framework for diagnosing insulation degradation and offers potential applications in condition monitoring and predictive maintenance of cast resin transformers.

Title: An Incipient Fault Detection Approach for Wind Turbine Generator Bearings Based on Speed-Normalized Morphological Filtering

Abstract: Operating under highly nonstationary conditions with frequent speed fluctuations, the condition monitoring of wind turbine generator (WTG) bearings presents a significant challenge. The results demonstrate that the presented HI delivers markedly enhanced detection capability for the incipient faults and outperforms the typical state-of-the-art HIs.

Title: Partial Discharge Anomaly Detection and Severity Assessment for HV Bushings Based on Self-Supervised Adversarial Encoder Network and Gaussian Mixture Model

To address these challenges, this paper proposes a PD anomaly detection and severity assessment method based on self-supervised adversarial encoder network and Gaussian mixture model (GMM). Unlike standard autoencoders that over-generalize, the Transformer-based adversarial encoder with dual competing decoders creates sharper anomaly boundaries, enabling high-sensitivity detection of weak PD signals without labeled data. Experimental results demonstrate effective PD detection across developmental stages, automatic severity identification, and quantitative condition assessment. Particularly when approaching critical states, the method captures significant anomaly score changes, enabling timely risk warnings. Compared with existing methods, this approach achieves high-precision detection without labeled data while providing adaptive severity assessment, offering significant practical value.

Title: A Two-Stage Hybrid Architecture for Unknown Anomaly Detection in Rotating Machinery Bearings
Authors: Ana Caroline Marques Costa; Pedro H.A.D. De Melo; Augusto Wohlgemuth Fleury Veloso Da Silveira; Marcelo Braga Dos Santos; Luciano Coutinho Gomes
Abstract: Supervised fault classifiers frequently encounter difficulties when dealing with faults that are not present in the training data, which is a prevalent issue in industrial contexts. To mitigate this limitation, we introduce a two-stage hybrid framework for diagnosing bearing fault. In the first stage, a supervised classifier assesses the posterior probability of each Known Fault class and predicts a Known Fault when its confidence exceeds a calibrated threshold τ. Samples with confidence below τ proceed to the second stage, where a one-class anomaly detector, trained solely on Normal Operation data, evaluates whether the sample aligns with normal behavior (Normal Operation) or deviates from it (Unknown Anomaly). This confidence-based routing produces three diagnostic outcomes: Normal Operation, Known Fault, and Unknown Anomaly, without necessitating retraining of the anomaly detector when new fault types are identified. Using the MAFAULDA dataset, which includes 41 experimental blocks covering closed-set, partial open-set, and fully open-set conditions, we evaluated supervised classifiers, deep learning architectures, and one-class detectors as potential candidates for each stage. Machine learning classifiers demonstrated superior performance compared to the deep learning architectures assessed, with the Isolation Forest proving to be the most effective one-class detector. Integrating the most robust classifier with the Isolation Forest under a calibrated confidence threshold enhanced the identification of previously unseen fault types compared to a baseline relying solely on supervised methods.

Title: Anomaly Detection in BLDC Motor using Machine Learning

Title: From Dataset to Deployment: A Full-Stack Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detection Pipeline for Gas Turbine BLDC Fuel Pumps
Authors: Viet Linh Nguyen; Duy Lanh Chu; Van Huy Nguyen
Abstract: Reliable health monitoring of fuel pumps is essential for maintaining the stability and safety of gas turbine engines. Brushless DC (BLDC) fuel pumps operate under tightly coupled electrical-mechanical-hydraulic dynamics, where fault progression is often subtle and real fault data are scarce. In offline analysis, the proposed autoencoder achieves competitive discrimination relative to strong unsupervised baselines, while its primary practical advantage lies in supporting a deterministic end-to-end TinyML deployment pipeline rather than maximizing offline discriminative performance alone. Under the current feature set and calibration, the evaluated partial-blockage and gradual-restriction scenarios did not produce persistence-triggered alarms, indicating incomplete fault-mode coverage and motivating future work on broader fault characterization and adaptive calibration. These results support the practical feasibility of real-time, on-device anomaly detection for gas-turbine fuel-pump monitoring in a resource-constrained TinyML setting.

Title: Detecting Anomalies Under Data Scarcity: Data Granularity Tradeoffs in Large Battery Packs
Authors: Matthias Wuest; Antoni Plonczak; Lilach Goren Huber
Abstract: As sensor-rich systems become increasingly prevalent, data-driven applications face growing pressure to balance information richness against practical constraints, such as storage, communication, and computational cost. This tension raises a fundamental question: how much data is enough? The challenge is particularly critical in anomaly detection (AD), where early identification of subtle deviations can prevent failures and safety incidents, yet excessive data collection may be infeasible. In this paper we study this tradeoff in the context of battery storage systems, a representative and safety-critical industrial application. Battery packs are composed of large numbers of electrically connected cells and can be monitored either at finegrained cell level or using aggregated pack-level measurements. While cell-level monitoring promises higher fidelity, most realworld systems rely on aggregated pack-level measurements due to scalability limitations. We systematically investigate whether access to fine-grained cell-level data consistently improves AD performance, or whether an intelligent selection of a small number of pack-level variables can achieve comparable results. We benchmark state-of-the-art deep learning-based AD methods against feature-engineering-based approaches under both data granularity assumptions. Furthermore, leveraging a highly flexible battery pack simulation framework, we analyze systematic differences between synthetic and real-world battery data, highlighting reality gaps that are often overlooked in AD research. Our results offer practical insights into data efficiency, model selection, and monitoring design, with implications that extend beyond batteries to a wide range of industrial condition monitoring applications.

Title: MSANet: Multi-Stage attention network for anomalous sound detection in machine condition monitoring
Authors: Hao Zhou; Yi Zhou; Yin Liu; Hongqing Liu
Abstract: Anomalous Sound Detection (ASD) system identifies sound waves from sensors to detect the anomaly of industrial machines. However, recent methods have failed to sufficiently focus on partial details and long-term dependence information in acoustic features, resulting in poor performance on certain machine types. To address this challenge, we propose a novel ASD model based on the multi-stage attention network (MSANet). The spectral-temporal concatenated spectrogram of the audio samples is used as the MSANet input, and serially modeled by the network. The fusion spectrogram attention network (FSAN) enhances inter-spectrogram correlation via directional pooling and attention weighting. Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is used in the local attention network to focus on the channel and spatial information in acoustic vectors, hence improving capacity of ASD system for modeling local information. In global attention network, the gated recurrent unit (GRU) is applied to improve the feed-forward layer of transformer, enhancing the model to capture global correlation feature and contextual information. Extensive experiments are conducted out on the DCASE 2020 Challenge Task 2 dataset to evaluate the proposed model. Experimental results demonstrate that MSANet achieves an average AUC of 94.89 % and an average pAUC of 89.11 %, both of which surpass the performance of previously methods.

Title: Pseudolabel-Guided Disentangled Representation Learning for Cross-Domain Anomalous Sound Detection

Title: Assessing the Feasibility of Transfer Learning from Metro Sensor Data to Telecommunication KPI Anomaly Detection

Abstract: The emergence of advance sensor data has led to considerable advancements in predictive maintenance (PdM) within metro systems, whereas energy and telecommunication infrastructures remain constrained by inadequately labelled fault data. This study examines the feasibility of transferring predictive maintenance knowledge from metro vehicles to data-scarce infrastructure domains using a transfer-learning framework. The MetroPT dataset was utilised and modelled using a supervised learning approach. The results show high in-domain accuracy of 98.8%, while the telecom baseline model achieved an accuracy of 0.9778 but exhibited low anomaly recall (0.125) reflecting the challenges associated with limited labelled fault data. These findings provide initial empirical evidence that direct model transfer between metro and telecom infrastructures is ineffective without appropriate domain alignment. The study therefore highlights the need for advanced adaptation techniques and domain-invariant representation learning to enable cross-sector PdM deployment in critical infrastructures.

Abstract: The connected vehicles create massive telematics data streams for predictive maintenance and safety monitoring. This work introduces real applications of quantum computing in automotive fleet management, and it also touches on large IoT pattern recognition challenges.

The proposed architecture combines various heterogeneous base learners, such as tree based models and temporal learning architecture to utilize that synergistic advantage of strength in statistical and sequential battery behaviour modelling. Title: Spectrogram-driven unsupervised autoencoder with isolation forest and one-class SVM for lab-scale wind turbine blade fault detection

Title: Self-Supervised Learning for Anomaly Detection in Gear Transmissions Using Vibration and Acoustic Signals
Authors: Kamil Musiał; Anna Burduk; M. Anthony Xavior; Suthep Butdee
Abstract: Gear units operate under highly dynamic loads and are prone to subtle defects such as tooth indentations, profile deviations, misalignment, and lack of lubrication. This study presents a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework for anomaly detection in production gear units, learning vibration and acoustic representations primarily from normal data without requiring fault-specific labels during training. An industrial case study is conducted on data from the final test stage collected at the gearbox manufacturing company. The dataset includes triaxial vibration signals, airborne acoustic signals and motor current signals for 1,200 helical gear units tested under three torque profiles. Learned embeddings are clustered to capture operational regimes, and anomalies are evaluated using density and probability-based models. The results indicate that SSL representations, together with simple clustering, provide a practical and interpretable approach to early defect detection in production settings. The study demonstrates that self-supervised representations can be integrated into existing quality control pipelines without requiring fault-specific training datasets.

Title: Anomaly Detection in Gas Turbines Based on Semisupervised Learning Framework

Authors: Primawati; Ferra Yanuar; Dodi Devianto; Remon Lapisa; Dwiprima Elvanny Myori; Fazrol Rozi

Title: Causal Learning for Fault and Anomaly Detection in Unmanned Aerial Systems
Authors: Atul Rawal
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) are vital to tactical autonomy applications, where they operate in contested, communication denied, and high stakes environments with limited human oversight. In such contexts, robust fault detection is not merely a safety concern but a mission critical capability where engine failures or control surface malfunctions can result in asset loss, mission failure, or compromised operational security. Traditional anomaly detection methods rely on correlation-based approaches that identify statistical deviations but fail to reveal the underlying causal mechanisms driving failures. This opacity is particularly problematic for tactical autonomy, where operators and commanders require explainable diagnostics to maintain situational awareness and trust in autonomous systems. We argue that causal learning provides a more principled and interpretable framework for understanding UAS faults. By utilizing causal learning to identify the cause-and-effect relations from telemetry data we can answer not only whether a fault occurred, but what caused it, enabling root cause analysis essential for rapid field assessment and informed decision making. We present preliminary proof-of-concept results using the ALFA (AirLab Failure and Anomaly) dataset to learn causal structures from UAS telemetry data. Our causal graphs reveal directional relationships between sensor readings, control inputs, and failure states, offering actionable insights for predictive maintenance, real time fault diagnosis, and post mission analysis that correlation-based methods cannot provide. We position causal reasoning as a foundational capability for trustworthy tactical autonomy.

Having labeled data on the dates when the pumps were operating abnormally, we are able to obtain the accuracy metrics on the anomaly detection performance of the METAL pipeline. Title: GenAD-SM: optimized transformer-VAE model for precision anomaly detection for smart manufacturing in industry 5.0
Authors: Surjeet Dalal; Umesh Kumar Lilhore; Sarita Simaiya; Deo Prakash; Sunita Yadav; Kuldeep Kumar; Ajay Kaushik
Abstract: Industry 5.0’s rapid smart manufacturing growth has increased demand for intelligent, resilient, and sustainable anomaly detection frameworks. Traditional machine learning methods require large labeled datasets, have low interpretability, scalability difficulties, and high processing costs, limiting their real-world usefulness. To counter balancing the experimental apparatus, erroneous conditions such as overheating, over-vibration and pressure dip were indicated against base operations. The FPOA-tuned VAE performed better than typical models as well as the Optuna baseline with F1-score of 0.983, AUC of 0.991 and accuracy of 0.982 and stable convergence between training and validation loss. The framework fosters human-centricity, resilience, and sustainability of Industry 5.0, as opposed to accuracy. The proposed model integrates technical innovation, social and ecological objectives, and explainability (through SHAP-based feature attributions), resistance to noisy inputs, and predictive maintenance, which reduces resource wastage. These findings indicate that FPOA-tuned VAE is a light, interpretable, and potent anomaly detecting framework of Industry 5.0 manufacturing.

An observer-based operating-condition labeling scheme and a noise-suppression strategy are further incorporated to ensure robust anomaly detection under varying speeds, loads, and measurement noise. In addition, long-term field deployment is conducted on two 15-kW cooling pump motors in a real industrial facility. The proposed EVCC framework successfully detects an abnormal operating event which cannot be identified by current-only AE method. These results demonstrate that voltage-guided current reconstruction provides enhanced visibility of electrical anomalies and offers a practical and effective solution for industrial motor condition monitoring.

Title: A Physics-Informed Spatiotemporal Framework for Automated Anomaly Detection in Intelligent in-Vehicle Displays
Authors: Wenning Xie; Ruiyuan Jiang; Fu Bi; Shuzhi Liu; Xinyi Zhao
Abstract: Driven by the rapid proliferation of connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs), the intelligent cockpit display system has emerged as a critical interface for delivering safety-critical information. However, display anomalies such as screen blackouts, flickering, and freezing usually introduce substantial safety hazards. Traditional computer vision methods are frequently hindered by the 'semantic ambiguity' between dark-themed user interfaces (UIs) and genuine black-screen faults. To address these limitations, we propose a novel dual-branch diagnostic framework. The static diagnostic branch employs a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) model, integrated with a spatial attention mechanism, to classify static anomalies (i.e., blue, black, blurred, and snow screens). Crucially, by incorporating a Sobel-based gradient constraint into the loss function, this branch effectively disentangles intentional dark UI designs from authentic hardware failures. The dynamic diagnostic branch utilizes a convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) to detect temporal faults, such as flickering and freezing, via sequence modeling. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness, offering a highly reliable solution for both automated end-of-line (EOL) testing and real-time in-vehicle health monitoring.

Title: Digital Twin Monitoring for Early Generator Fault Detection in Utility-Scale Wind Turbines

Abstract: Early detection of generator thermal faults in wind turbines remains challenging because conventional threshold-based monitoring typically identifies faults only after significant degradation has occurred. Title: Scale-Compensation Community Distance Entropy: A Novel Feature Extraction Tool for Fault Identification of Rotating Machinery
Authors: Chenyang Ma; Zhiqiang Cai; Ke Feng; Yimeng Wang; Yongbo Li
Abstract: Fault identification plays a pivotal role in condition-based maintenance of rotating machinery, with identification accuracy highly dependent on the quality of extracted features. However, PE is unresponsive to amplitude variation due to the binary orbit similarity state, and the multiscale procedure suffers from scale information loss or even scale absence, all of which decrease the identification accuracy. On one hand, the community distance-based orbit similarity value is put forward to diversify orbit similarity states, achieving a dual-characteristic perception of both frequency and amplitude changes. On the other hand, the scale-compensation procedure is proposed to enrich overall and detailed information on continuous scales. The efficiency and superiority of SCDE are rigorously demonstrated using simulation data and experimental datasets.

Title: AI-Based Hydraulic and Electrical Fault Identification in Direct-Driven Hydraulic Systems

Abstract: Direct drive hydraulic (DDH) systems present a promising alternative to traditional systems in off-road mobile machinery (NRMM) due to their energy efficiency, improved controllability, and lower maintenance costs. The obtained results prove the effectiveness and prospects of the proposed fault diagnosis method in both DDH and other electro-hydraulic systems. Such a method can increase the probability of timely fault detection, thereby reducing downtime and maintenance costs while significantly increasing the efficiency of NRMM.

Abstract: To address the limitations of traditional singlesensor monitoring in wind turbines - such as limited data dimensions, high hidden hazard detection rates, and insufficient health assessment accuracy - the study proposes a multi-sensor data fusion-based method for hidden hazard feature extraction and health evaluation. By constructing a LSTM-Transformerbased health assessment model, the method achieves quantitative evaluation of key component degradation and prediction of remaining service life. Validation results demonstrate that compared to conventional single-sensor diagnostics, this approach improves hidden hazard recognition accuracy to 89.7%, extends gearbox fault warning time windows to 142 hours, and maintains root mean square error (RMSE) in health status assessments below 3.2%. The findings indicate that multi-sensor data fusion technology significantly enhances the reliability of hidden hazard identification and health assessment for wind turbines, providing technical support for predictive maintenance in wind farms.

Title: Machine Fault Identification Using a Digital Twin-Based Augmented Vision Framework with IoT-Enabled Sensors
Authors: K. Elavarasi; Z. Mohammed Javith; N. Imran; K. Rajkumar
Abstract: In modern industries, machines serve as the backbone of production. Any unexpected downtime can lead to a complete halt in operations, resulting in significant losses in productivity and revenue. Ensuring the continuous and efficient operation of machinery is therefore a critical aspect of industrial maintenance. The proposed system introduces a Digital Twin (DT)-based Augmented Vision (AV) framework designed to support predictive maintenance by integrating IoT-enabled sensors, real-time visualization, and fault diagnostics. The system employs a DT scanner to capture and visualize the operating condition of machines, providing a color-coded output - green for normal, orange for warning, and red for critical conditions such as abnormal vibration, overcurrent, overheating, or excessive noise. The approach combines IoT-based data acquisition with DT visualization to deliver an intelligent, low-cost, and efficient solution for monitoring and maintaining industrial equipment. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed system improves diagnostic accuracy, reduces service time, and ensures enhanced operational reliability environments.

Title: Hybrid Late-Fusion Approach for Intelligent Fault Identification Under Cross-Load Operating Conditions
Authors: Knap Paweł; Jachymczyk Urszula
Abstract: This paper addresses several practical gaps in intelligent fault identification of rotating machinery: 1) limited cross-load generalization, 2) lack of interpretability of data-driven models, and 3) overly optimistic results caused by weakly controlled testing protocols. We propose a relatively simple hybrid late-fusion framework that combines a deep learning branch operating on raw vibration signals with a conventional machine-learning branch trained on handcrafted condition indicators. The two branches are fused at the decision level using a stacking meta-classifier, which enables both performance gains and explicit analysis of the fusion mechanism. On a dedicated laboratory test rig evaluated in a cross-load setting (training at no-load and testing at load of 4 Nm), the condition indicators-based Machine Learning (ML) model alone achieves an accuracy of approximately 83.4%, while the deep 1D-CNN branch reaches about 86.7%. The proposed stacking-based late fusion with a Radial Basis Function Support Vector Classifier (RBF-SVC) meta-classifier increases the accuracy to 92.2%, with consistent improvements in F1-score and AUC. Additional experiments on the widely used Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset yield 100% accuracy, confirming that the proposed architecture remains competitive on standard benchmarks while its main benefits appear under realistic operating-condition shifts. To improve interpretability, we perform an extensive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis of both the ML branch and the stacking meta-model. The results link the decisions to physically meaningful condition indicators and show how the meta-classifier integrates deep and classical predictions, providing an explicit, quantitative explanation of the hybrid model's behaviour.

Title: A Lightweight Transformer-Based Early-Stage Fault Identification Method for Tunnel Boring Machine Main Bearings with Limited Data
Authors: Zhiyao Zhang; Mengqi Zhang; Jiliang Mo; Yuanyuan Mei; Hongtao Shi; Longguan Zhang
Abstract: Tunnel boring machine (TBM) main bearings are critical components that require continuous condition monitoring but are physically inaccessible during tunneling. They feature ultralarge structural dimensions, ultralow speeds, and alternating loads, creating extreme operational conditions. These factors lead to exceptionally weak, rapidly attenuated vibration signatures and severe difficulty in acquiring labeled measurement data. Conventional vibration-based diagnostic methods struggle to achieve reliable early-stage fault identification under these constraints. To address this, we propose ASAFormer, a lightweight Transformer-based measurement framework designed for weak-signal enhancement and data-efficient fault identification. ASAFormer integrates two core modules: the weak-signal aware sparse attention (WSASA) leverages token-level variance modulation with single-head sparse attention to selectively amplify low-energy transient features while suppressing noise. The selective convolutional knowledge distillation (SCKD) module extracts multiscale local patterns through parallel convolutional filters and selectively distills the most discriminative measurement features. Stacking WSASA and SCKD builds a hierarchical representation that fuses global weak-signal awareness with local sensitivity under severe noise and data scarcity. Experimental validation on a custom-designed TBM main bearing test rig demonstrates the feasibility of this measurement-driven approach for early-stage fault identification. ASAFormer achieves over 90.5% accuracy with only 100 samples per class and maintains performance stability when training data is halved.

Title: Modeling of a flexible slider-crank mechanism with unbalance: A neural network-based inverse dynamics approach for fault identification
Authors: Abdullah Mohammed; Khalid Alghanim; Abdulazim Falah
Abstract: This study presents a neural network-based inverse dynamics method for identifying unbalance faults in flexible slider-crank mechanisms. Slider-crank mechanisms are central in reciprocating machinery, and their dynamics can be altered by unbalance and link flexibility. We develop a Lagrangian model of a flexible slider-crank with an extensible spring-damper connecting link and a parametric unbalance mass on a triangular plate, then train a feedforward neural network to recover five coupled physical parameters (unbalance mass, angular position, eccentricity, period time, and damping ratio) simultaneously from a single 51-point displacement trace. On clean synthetic data, the network achieves R >0.97 for all five parameters with sub-millisecond inference. A spatial error analysis maps prediction accuracy to unbalance position on the link, revealing that errors concentrate near the crank and slider joints where kinematic sensitivity is lowest. A noise robustness study shows that the clean-data network fails entirely under measurement noise; retraining with noise-augmented data (30–60 dB SNR) restores useful accuracy for four parameters at realistic noise levels, while unbalance mass remains vulnerable due to its weak coupling to slider displacement. These results establish quantitative bounds on the method’s applicability and identify supplementary sensing requirements for experimental implementation.

Title: A Cost-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Gearbox Fault Detection in Wind Turbines
Authors: Morten Lindberg Larsen; Rasmus Dovnborg Frederiksen; Alex Elkjær Vasegaard; Peter Nielsen
Abstract: The maintenance operations in the wind sector (particularly offshore) are extremely costly, and thus technologies for optimization of maintenance need to take the high risks related to these costs into account. On the topic of predictive maintenance, any false prediction can lead to high cost incursions, and even a few false predictions can invalidate the predictive maintenance strategy. The costs and benefits of correct and false predictions are not uniform or symmetric, leading the conventional performance metrics to misalign the perceived model performance with the actual business impact. This problem leads us to introduce a cost-aware deep learning framework that accounts for the costs and benefits of predictions. This framework is achieved by loss functions designed to adjust the parameters according to the cost–benefit and not to optimize model accuracy. For the case study of wind turbine generator gearbox failure prediction, several cost-aware loss functions are tested, along with a novel fine-tuning approach that combines them. The case study shows that using cost-aware expected-value loss functions improves cost–benefit performance by an average of 30–57% compared with models trained with conventional loss functions.

Title: A comprehensive wind turbine digital model approach for drive-train broken tooth-type fault detection
Authors: Deiver Jiménez-Santín; Mariela Cerrada; Josué Enríquez-Zárate; Diego Cabrera; René Vinicio Sánchez
Abstract: This paper presents a modular Digital Model of a wind turbine drive-train explicitly oriented toward the physical analysis and detection of broken tooth faults in the third gearbox stage. The model integrates aerodynamic, drive-train, generator, and control subsystems under a set of deliberate simplifying assumptions that define a controlled and physically interpretable reference framework. To isolate fault-related mechanisms, the first two gearbox stages are aggregated, while the third stage is modeled in detail using a lumped-parameter formulation with time-varying mesh stiffness and viscous damping. Tooth breakage is represented as a periodic reduction in effective contact width through a square-wave approximation. Under turbulent wind conditions and partial-load operation, simulations are conducted for healthy and progressively degraded scenarios. The results show that frequency-domain indicators, including gear-mesh sideband amplitudes and global spectral energy, exhibit clear and monotonic sensitivity to fault severity. Complementary time-domain statistical features, particularly RMS, variance, skewness, and rectified mean value, demonstrate strong monotonicity, trendability, and prognostic ability once damage reaches moderate levels. Overall, the proposed Digital Model functions as a baseline platform for mechanistically interpretable drive-train fault analysis and supports systematic experimental ablations. Its modular structure enables future extensions toward increased model complexity, experimental validation, and the development of data-synchronized Digital Twins for condition monitoring and Remaining Useful Life estimation.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Wind Power Forecasting and Automated Fault Detection Using SCADA Data
Authors: Sude Ozcan; Ibraheem Shayea; Gul Gabdulualitovna Dzhussupova; Kassimova Botakoz Rahmetollaevna; Leila Rzayeva
Abstract: This paper outlines a dual-phase machine learning-based method for predicting wind energy production, and automatically detecting faults within those predictions based on a large data set of approximately 65,000 operational records of a large commercial scale on-shore wind turbine. In the first phase of this study, two types of supervised machine learning algorithms were used to predict the active power produced by the turbine given inputs regarding meteorological conditions and mechanical operations. These two predictive models include a Random Forest Regressor model which achieved an R-squared score of 0.962; however, demonstrated increased ability to withstand rapid changes in wind speed. In addition, an Artificial Neural Network model was developed and provided comparable accuracy when there were no significant changes in either the weather or turbine operation. In the second phase, the same data were analyzed using an Isolation Forest algorithm to identify anomalies in both the predicted and theoretical power output values. Those anomalies were defined as the residual value associated with each data point representing the difference between the amount of electricity being generated at a particular time and what should be generated given typical operating parameters. Anomalies identified using the Isolation Forest algorithm included 420 unique anomalous situations that were correctly identified 94 % of the time and accurately classified using the F1-score metric. The correlations between these anomalies and abnormal operating conditions such as gearbox oil temperatures, generator RPMs, etc., are strong evidence of their relevance. By integrating forecasting and anomaly detection into a single process flow, this work has shown that it is possible to provide significantly higher levels of reliability compared to using one of these processes independently. As a result, this technology can enable proactive maintenance decisions that will ultimately help extend the life expectancy of equipment and minimize unplanned outages in today's wind farms.
